verses.1:1: After the death of Joshua, the sons of Israel consulted the Lord, saying, "Who will go up before us against the Canaanites and be the leader of the war?"
verses.1:2: And the Lord said, "Judah will go up; look, I have handed the land over into his hands."
verses.1:3: And Judah said to his brother Simeon, "Go up with me into my lot and fight against the Canaanites, so that I also may go with you into your lot." And Simeon went with him.
verses.1:4: And Judah went up, and the Lord handed the Canaanites and the Perizzites over into their hands; and they struck down ten thousand men in Bezek.
verses.1:5: And they found Adoni-bezek in Bezek, and fought against him, and struck down the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
verses.1:6: But Adoni-bezek fled; and they pursued and captured him, cutting off the extremities of his hands and feet.
verses.1:7: And Adoni-bezek said, "Seventy kings, with the extremities of their hands and feet cut off, used to gather scraps of food under my table; just as I have done, so God has repaid me." And they brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.
verses.1:8: Therefore, attacking Jerusalem, the sons of Judah captured it and struck it by the edge of the sword, handing the entire city over to fire.
verses.1:9: And afterward, going down, they fought against the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, and toward the south, and in the plains.
verses.1:10: And Judah, advancing against the Canaanites who lived in Hebron (whose name in ancient times was Kiriath-arba), struck down Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai;
verses.1:11: and setting out from there, he went to the inhabitants of Debir, whose old name was Kiriath-sepher, that is, the city of letters.
verses.1:12: And Caleb said, "Whoever strikes Kiriath-sepher and lays it waste, to him I will give my daughter Achsah as a wife."
verses.1:13: And when Othniel the son of Kenaz, the younger brother of Caleb, had captured it, he gave him his daughter Achsah as his wife.
verses.1:14: As she was going along the way, her husband advised her to ask her father for a field. And when she sighed while sitting on the donkey, Caleb said to her, "What is the matter with you?"
verses.1:15: But she answered, "Give me a blessing, because you have given me a dry land; give me also one watered with waters." Therefore Caleb gave her the upper watered ground and the lower watered ground.
verses.1:16: Now the sons of the Kenite, the relative of Moses, went up from the city of palms with the sons of Judah into the wilderness of his lot, which is south of Arad, and lived with him.
verses.1:17: And Judah went with his brother Simeon, and together they struck down the Canaanites who lived in Zephath and killed them. And the name of the city was called Hormah, that is, anathema.
verses.1:18: And Judah captured Gaza with its borders, and Ashkelon, and Ekron with its boundaries.
verses.1:19: And the Lord was with Judah, and he possessed the hill country; nor was he able to wipe out the inhabitants of the valley, because they abounded in scythed chariots.
verses.1:20: And just as Moses had said, they gave Hebron to Caleb, who wiped out the three sons of Anak from it.
verses.1:21: However, the sons of Benjamin did not wipe out the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and the Jebusites have lived with the sons of Benjamin in Jerusalem to the present day.
verses.1:22: The house of Joseph also went up to Bethel, and the Lord was with them.
verses.1:23: For while they were besieging the city, which was formerly called Luz,
verses.1:24: they saw a man coming out of the city, and said to him, "Show us the entrance of the city, and we will show mercy to you."
verses.1:25: And when he had shown it to them, they struck the city by the edge of the sword; but they let that man and all his family go.
verses.1:26: And having been released, he went into the land of the Hittites, and built a city there, and called it Luz, which is so called to the present day.
verses.1:27: Manasseh also did not wipe out Beth-shean and Taanach with their villages, nor the inhabitants of Dor, and Ibleam, and Megiddo with their villages; and the Canaanites began to live with them.
verses.1:28: And after Israel grew strong, he made them tributaries, and was unwilling to wipe them out.
verses.1:29: Ephraim also did not kill the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, but lived with them.
verses.1:30: Zebulun did not wipe out the inhabitants of Kitron and Nahalol; instead, the Canaanites lived in his midst and became tributary to him.
verses.1:31: Asher also did not wipe out the inhabitants of Acco and of Sidon, Ahlab, and Achzib, and Helbah, and Aphek, and Rehob;
verses.1:32: and he lived in the midst of the Canaanites, the inhabitants of that land, nor did he kill them.
verses.1:33: Naphtali also did not wipe out the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath; and he lived among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land, and the Beth-shemites and the Beth-anathites became tributary to him.
verses.1:34: And the Amorites confined the sons of Dan to the hill country, and did not give them room to come down to the flatter areas;
verses.1:35: and they lived on Mount Heres, which is translated as earthen, in Aijalon and Shaalbim. And the hand of the house of Joseph grew heavy, and they became tributary to it.
verses.1:36: Now the boundary of the Amorites was from the ascent of the Scorpion, the rock, and the higher places.
verses.2:1: And the angel of the Lord went up from Gilgal to the Place of Those Who Weep, and said, "I led you out of Egypt, and brought you into the land concerning which I swore to your fathers; and I promised that I would not make My covenant with you void forever,
verses.2:2: provided only that you would not strike a covenant with the inhabitants of this land, but would overthrow their altars; yet you were unwilling to listen to My voice. Why have you done this?
verses.2:3: For this reason I was unwilling to wipe them out from before your face, so that you may have enemies, and their gods may be a ruin to you."
verses.2:4: And as the angel of the Lord spoke these words to all the sons of Israel, they lifted up their voice and wept.
verses.2:5: And the name of that place was called the Place of Those Who Weep, or of Tears; and there they offered sacrifices of the Lord.
verses.2:6: Therefore Joshua dismissed the people, and the sons of Israel went away, each one to his own possession, to obtain it;
verses.2:7: and they served the Lord all his days, and those of the elders who lived for a long time after him and knew all the works of the Lord that He had done with Israel.
verses.2:8: Now Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died at one hundred and ten years of age,
verses.2:9: and they buried him within the borders of his possession in Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim, on the northern side of Mount Gaash.
verses.2:10: And all that generation was gathered to their fathers; and others arose who did not know the Lord or the works that He had done with Israel.
verses.2:11: And the sons of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and served the Baals.
verses.2:12: And they abandoned the Lord God of their fathers, who had led them out of the land of Egypt, and followed foreign gods and the gods of the peoples who lived around them, and worshiped them; and they provoked the Lord to anger,
verses.2:13: abandoning Him and serving Baal and Ashtaroth.
verses.2:14: And becoming angry against Israel, the Lord handed them over into the hands of plunderers, who captured them and sold them to the enemies who lived all around; nor were they able to resist their adversaries,
verses.2:15: but wherever they wished to go, the hand of the Lord was upon them, just as He spoke and swore to them, and they were severely afflicted.
verses.2:16: And the Lord raised up judges to rescue them from the hands of those who ravaged them; yet they were unwilling to listen even to them,
verses.2:17: fornicating with foreign gods and worshiping them. Quickly they deserted the way by which their fathers had walked; and hearing the commands of the Lord, they did everything to the contrary.
verses.2:18: And whenever the Lord raised up judges, in their days He was moved with mercy, and heard the groans of the afflicted, and rescued them from the slaughter of those who ravaged them.
verses.2:19: But after the judge had died, they turned back and did much worse things than their fathers had done, following foreign gods, serving them, and worshiping them. They did not abandon their own devices, nor the most stubborn way along which they were accustomed to walk.
verses.2:20: And the fury of the Lord was aroused against Israel, and He said, "Because this nation has made My covenant void, which I had made with their fathers, and has scorned to listen to My voice,
verses.2:21: I also will not wipe out the nations that Joshua left behind when he died,
verses.2:22: so that through them I may test Israel, whether they keep the way of the Lord and walk in it, just as their fathers kept it, or not."
verses.2:23: Therefore the Lord left all these nations, and was unwilling to overthrow them quickly, nor did He hand them over into the hands of Joshua.
verses.3:1: These are the nations that the Lord left behind so that He might instruct Israel through them, and all who had not known the wars of the Canaanites,
verses.3:2: so that afterward their sons might learn to fight with enemies and to have the practice of waging war:
verses.3:3: the five satraps of the Philistines, and every Canaanite, and the Sidonian, and the Hivite who lived on Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal-hermon as far as the entrance of Hamath.
verses.3:4: And He left them so that through them He might test Israel, whether they would listen to the commandments of the Lord that He had commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses, or not.
verses.3:5: So the sons of Israel lived in the midst of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite;
verses.3:6: and they took their daughters as wives, and they themselves gave their own daughters to their sons, and they served their gods.
verses.3:7: And they did evil in the sight of the Lord, and they forgot their God, serving the Baals and Ashtaroth.
verses.3:8: And angered against Israel, the Lord handed them over into the hands of Cushan-rishathaim, king of Mesopotamia, and they served him for eight years.
verses.3:9: And they cried out to the Lord, who raised up a savior for them and delivered them, namely, Othniel the son of Kenaz, the younger brother of Caleb.
verses.3:10: And the Spirit of the Lord was in him, and he judged Israel. And he went out to battle, and the Lord handed over into his hands Cushan-rishathaim, king of Syria, and he overpowered him.
verses.3:11: And the land rested for forty years, and Othniel the son of Kenaz died.
verses.3:12: Now the sons of Israel again did evil in the sight of the Lord, who strengthened Eglon, king of Moab, against them, because they did evil in His sight.
verses.3:13: And He joined to him the sons of Ammon and Amalek; and he went and struck Israel, and took possession of the city of palms.
verses.3:14: And the sons of Israel served Eglon, king of Moab, for eighteen years.
verses.3:15: And afterward they cried out to the Lord, who raised up for them a savior named Ehud, the son of Gera, the son of Jemini, who used either hand as a right hand. And the sons of Israel sent gifts through him to Eglon, king of Moab.
verses.3:16: And he made for himself a double-edged sword, having in the middle a hilt the length of the palm of a hand, and he fastened it on beneath his cloak on his right thigh.
verses.3:17: And he presented the gifts to Eglon, king of Moab. Now Eglon was exceedingly fat.
verses.3:18: And when he had presented the gifts to him, he escorted the companions who had come with him.
verses.3:19: And having returned from Gilgal, where the idols were, he said to the king, "I have a secret word for you, king." And he commanded silence; and when all who were around him had gone out,
verses.3:20: Ehud went in to him; now he was sitting alone in the summer upper room; and he said, "I have a word of God for you." And he immediately rose from the throne.
verses.3:21: And Ehud stretched out his left hand and took the dagger from his right thigh, and drove it into his belly
verses.3:22: so forcefully that the hilt followed the blade into the wound and was gripped tightly by the thickest fat. Nor did he draw out the sword, but just as he had struck, he left it in the body; and immediately through the secret passages of nature the excrement of the bowels burst forth.
verses.3:23: Now Ehud, having very carefully closed the doors of the upper room and secured them with the bolt,
verses.3:24: went out through the back door. And the servants of the king came in and saw the doors of the upper room closed, and they said, "Perhaps he is emptying his bowels in the summer chamber."
verses.3:25: And waiting a long time until they were embarrassed, and seeing that no one was opening them, they took the key; and opening them, they found their lord lying dead on the ground.
verses.3:26: Meanwhile Ehud, while they were in confusion, escaped and passed by the place of the idols from which he had turned back. And he came to Seirah,
verses.3:27: and immediately he sounded the trumpet in Mount Ephraim, and the sons of Israel went down with him, while he himself marched at the front.
verses.3:28: And he said to them, "Follow me, for the Lord has handed over our enemies the Moabites into our hands." And they went down after him and seized the fords of the Jordan that lead across into Moab, and they did not allow anyone to cross over;
verses.3:29: rather, they struck down the Moabites at that time, about ten thousand, all sturdy and strong men. Not one of them was able to escape.
verses.3:30: And Moab was humbled on that day under the hand of Israel, and the land rested for eighty years.
verses.3:31: After him was Shamgar the son of Anath, who struck down six hundred men of the Philistines with a plowshare; and he also defended Israel.
verses.4:1: And the sons of Israel again did evil in the sight of the Lord after the death of Ehud,
verses.4:2: and the Lord handed them over into the hands of Jabin, king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor; and he had a commander of his army named Sisera, and he himself lived in Harosheth of the nations.
verses.4:3: And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord, for he had nine hundred scythed chariots, and for twenty years he had severely oppressed them.
verses.4:4: Now there was Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, who judged the people at that time.
verses.4:5: And she sat under the palm tree that was called by her name, between Ramah and Bethel in Mount Ephraim; and the sons of Israel went up to her for every judgment.
verses.4:6: And she sent and summoned Barak the son of Abinoam from Kedesh-naphtali, and she said to him, "The Lord God of Israel has commanded you: 'Go and lead an army to Mount Tabor, and you will take with you ten thousand fighters from the sons of Naphtali and from the sons of Zebulun;
verses.4:7: and I will bring to you, at the place of the torrent Kishon, Sisera, the chief of Jabin's army, and his chariots and all the multitude, and I will hand them over into your hand.'"
verses.4:8: And Barak said to her, "If you come with me, I will go; if you are unwilling to come with me, I will not go on."
verses.4:9: And she said to him, "I will indeed go with you, but on this occasion the victory will not be credited to you, because Sisera will be handed over into the hand of a woman." So Deborah rose and went on with Barak to Kedesh.
verses.4:10: And he, having summoned Zebulun and Naphtali, went up with ten thousand fighters, having Deborah in his company.
verses.4:11: Now Heber the Kenite had formerly withdrawn from the rest of the Kenites, his brothers, the sons of Hobab, the relative of Moses, and had pitched his tents as far as the valley that is called Sennim, and it was near Kedesh.
verses.4:12: And it was reported to Sisera that Barak the son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor;
verses.4:13: and he gathered nine hundred scythed chariots and all the army from Harosheth of the nations to the torrent Kishon.
verses.4:14: And Deborah said to Barak, "Rise, for this is the day on which the Lord has handed over Sisera into your hands; look, He Himself is your leader." So Barak went down from Mount Tabor, and ten thousand fighters with him.
verses.4:15: And the Lord terrified Sisera, and all his chariots, and the entire multitude by the edge of the sword at the sight of Barak, to such an extent that Sisera, leaping down from his chariot, fled on foot,
verses.4:16: and Barak pursued the fleeing chariots and the army as far as Harosheth of the nations, and the entire multitude of the enemies fell to utter destruction.
verses.4:17: Now Sisera, fleeing, reached the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite. For there was peace between Jabin, king of Hazor, and the house of Heber the Kenite.
verses.4:18: Therefore Jael went out to meet Sisera and said to him, "Come in to me, my lord; come in, do not be afraid." And having entered her tent and been covered by her with a cloak,
verses.4:19: he said to her, "Give me, I beg you, a little water, because I am very thirsty." And she opened a skin of milk and gave him a drink, and she covered him.
verses.4:20: And Sisera said to her, "Stand before the entrance of the tent; and when someone comes questioning you and saying, 'Is anyone here?' you will answer, 'There is no one.'"
verses.4:21: Therefore Jael, the wife of Heber, took a tent peg, taking along a hammer as well; and having gone in secretly and in silence, she placed the peg upon the temple of his head, and striking it with the hammer, she drove it into his brain all the way to the ground; and he, uniting deep sleep with death, fainted and died.
verses.4:22: And look, Barak was coming, following Sisera; and Jael went out to meet him and said to him, "Come, and I will show you the man whom you are seeking." And when he had gone in to her, he saw Sisera lying dead, and the peg driven into his temple.
verses.4:23: Therefore God humbled Jabin, king of Canaan, on that day before the sons of Israel,
verses.4:24: who grew daily and with a strong hand oppressed Jabin, king of Canaan, until they destroyed him.
verses.5:1: And Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam sang on that day, saying:
verses.5:2: "You of Israel who willingly offered your lives to danger, bless the Lord.
verses.5:3: Hear, kings; give ear, princes: it is I, it is I, who will sing to the Lord; I will sing praises to the Lord, the God of Israel.
verses.5:4: Lord, when You went out from Seir and passed through the regions of Edom, the earth was shaken, and the heavens and the clouds dripped with waters.
verses.5:5: The mountains flowed before the face of the Lord, and Sinai before the face of the Lord, the God of Israel.
verses.5:6: In the days of Shamgar the son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the paths rested, and those who traveled along them walked along out-of-the-way tracks.
verses.5:7: The mighty men in Israel ceased and rested, until Deborah arose, arose as a mother in Israel.
verses.5:8: The Lord chose new wars, and He Himself overthrew the gates of the enemies; if shield and spear appeared among forty thousand of Israel.
verses.5:9: My heart loves the princes of Israel; you who of your own will offered yourselves to peril, bless the Lord.
verses.5:10: You who ride on gleaming donkeys, and sit in judgment, and walk along the way, speak.
verses.5:11: Where the chariots were smashed together and the army of the enemies was suffocated, there let the righteous deeds of the Lord be recounted, and clemency toward the mighty men of Israel; then the people of the Lord went down to the gates and obtained dominion.
verses.5:12: Arise, arise, Deborah; arise, arise, and speak a song; arise, Barak, and seize your captives, son of Abinoam.
verses.5:13: The remnant of the people was saved; the Lord fought among the mighty men.
verses.5:14: Out of Ephraim He destroyed them in Amalek, and after him out of Benjamin against your peoples, Amalek; from Machir princes came down, and from Zebulun those who would lead the army to wage war.
verses.5:15: The leaders of Issachar were with Deborah, and they followed the footsteps of Barak, who gave himself over to peril as if into a precipice and an abyss; with Reuben divided against himself, a contention of great-hearted men was found.
verses.5:16: Why do you dwell between two borders, to hear the whistlings of the flocks? With Reuben divided against himself, a contention of great-hearted men was found.
verses.5:17: Gilead rested beyond the Jordan, and Dan was occupied with ships; Asher dwelt on the shore of the sea and stayed in the harbors.
verses.5:18: But Zebulun and Naphtali offered their lives to death in the region of Merome.
verses.5:19: The kings came and fought; the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach beside the waters of Megiddo, and yet they carried off nothing while plundering.
verses.5:20: From heaven battle was fought against them; the stars, remaining in their order and course, fought against Sisera.
verses.5:21: The torrent of Kishon dragged away their corpses, the torrent of Kedumim, the torrent of Kishon; trample down the strong, my soul.
verses.5:22: The hooves of the horses fell off as the mightiest of the enemies fled in a rush and plunged headlong.
verses.5:23: 'Curse the land of Meroz,' said the angel of the Lord, 'curse its inhabitants, because they did not come to the help of the Lord, to the assistance of His mightiest ones.'
verses.5:24: Blessed among women be Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, and may she be blessed in her tent.
verses.5:25: To him who asked for water she gave milk, and in a bowl of princes she offered butter.
verses.5:26: She put her left hand to the peg and her right hand to the hammers of craftsmen. And she struck Sisera, seeking in his head a place for the wound, and forcefully piercing through his temple;
verses.5:27: between her feet he collapsed; he fainted and died; he rolled before her feet and lay lifeless and wretched.
verses.5:28: Looking out through the window, his mother wailed, and from the upper room she spoke: 'Why does his chariot delay in returning? Why have the feet of his four-horse chariots been slow?'
verses.5:29: One wiser than the rest of his wives answered her mother-in-law with these words:
verses.5:30: 'Perhaps he is now dividing the spoils, and the most beautiful of the women is being chosen for him; garments of diverse colors are being handed over to Sisera as plunder, and varied finery is being gathered to adorn necks.'
verses.5:31: So may all Your enemies perish, Lord; but those who love You, just as the sun shines at its rising, so may they shine brightly."
verses.6:1: Now the sons of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, who handed them over into the hand of Midian for seven years,
verses.6:2: and they were greatly oppressed by them. And they made for themselves dens and caves in the mountains, and very strongly fortified places for resisting.
verses.6:3: And whenever Israel had sown, Midian and Amalek and the rest of the eastern nations would come up,
verses.6:4: and pitching their tents among them, they would lay waste everything just as it was in the green shoots, as far as the entrance of Gaza; and they would leave nothing at all pertaining to life in Israel, neither sheep, nor oxen, nor donkeys.
verses.6:5: For they themselves and all their flocks would come with their tents, and like locusts they would fill everything, a countless multitude of men and camels, devastating whatever they had touched.
verses.6:6: And Israel was greatly humbled in the sight of Midian.
verses.6:7: And they cried out to the Lord, asking for help against the Midianites.
verses.6:8: And He sent to them a man, a prophet, and he spoke: "This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: I caused you to go up from Egypt, and I led you out of the house of slavery,
verses.6:9: and I delivered you from the hand of the Egyptians and of all the enemies who were afflicting you; and I drove them out at your entrance and gave their land to you.
verses.6:10: And I said, 'I am the Lord your God; do not fear the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell.' And you were unwilling to listen to My voice."
verses.6:11: Now the angel of the Lord came and sat under an oak that was in Ophrah and belonged to Joash, the father of the family of Ezri. And while his son Gideon was beating out and cleaning grain in a winepress in order to flee from Midian,
verses.6:12: the angel of the Lord appeared to him and said, "The Lord is with you, mightiest of men."
verses.6:13: And Gideon said to him, "Please, my lord, if the Lord is with us, why have all these things overtaken us? Where are His wonders, which our fathers recounted and said, 'The Lord led us out of Egypt'? But now the Lord has abandoned us and handed us over into the hand of Midian."
verses.6:14: And the Lord looked at him and said, "Go in this strength of yours, and you will deliver Israel from the hand of Midian; know that I have sent you."
verses.6:15: He answered and said, "Please, my lord, with what will I deliver Israel? Look, my family is the lowest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house."
verses.6:16: And the Lord said to him, "I will be with you, and you will strike Midian as one man."
verses.6:17: And he said, "If I have found favor before You, give me a sign that it is You who are speaking to me,
verses.6:18: and do not depart from here until I return to You, bringing a sacrifice and offering it to You." And He answered, "I will wait for your coming."
verses.6:19: So Gideon went inside and cooked a young goat, and unleavened loaves from a measure of flour; and putting the meat in a basket and pouring the broth of the meat into a pot, he carried it all under the oak and offered it to Him.
verses.6:20: And the angel of the Lord said to him, "Take the meat and the unleavened loaves, and place them upon that rock, and pour the broth over them." And when he had done so,
verses.6:21: the angel of the Lord stretched out the tip of the staff that he held in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened loaves; and fire went up from the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened loaves; and the angel of the Lord vanished from his eyes.
verses.6:22: And Gideon, seeing that it was the angel of the Lord, said, "Alas, my Lord God! For I have seen the angel of the Lord face to face."
verses.6:23: And the Lord said to him, "Peace be with you; do not fear, you will not die."
verses.6:24: Therefore Gideon built an altar there to the Lord and called it "The Lord's Peace," until the present day. And while he was still in Ophrah, which belongs to the family of Ezri,
verses.6:25: on that night the Lord said to him, "Take your father's bull and a second bull, seven years old, and you will destroy the altar of Baal that belongs to your father, and cut down the grove that is around the altar.
verses.6:26: And you will build an altar to the Lord your God on the top of this rock, upon which you placed the sacrifice before; and you will take the second bull and offer a burnt offering upon the pile of wood that you have cut down from the grove."
verses.6:27: Therefore Gideon, having taken ten men from his servants, did just as the Lord had commanded him. However, fearing his father's house and the men of that city, he was unwilling to do it by day, but completed everything by night.
verses.6:28: And when the men of his town rose in the morning, they saw the altar of Baal destroyed, and the sacred grove cut down, and the second bull placed upon the altar that had then been built.
verses.6:29: And they said to one another, "Who did this?" And when they inquired about the author of the deed, it was said, "Gideon the son of Joash did all these things."
verses.6:30: And they said to Joash, "Bring your son out here, so that he may die, because he destroyed the altar of Baal and cut down the grove."
verses.6:31: And he answered them, "Are you the avengers of Baal, that you should fight for him? Whoever is his adversary, let him die before tomorrow's light comes. If he is a god, let him avenge himself on the one who undermined his altar."
verses.6:32: From that day Gideon was called Jerubbaal, because Joash had said, "Let Baal avenge himself on the one who undermined his altar."
verses.6:33: Therefore all Midian and Amalek and the eastern peoples were gathered together, and crossing the Jordan, they encamped in the valley of Jezreel.
verses.6:34: Now the Spirit of the Lord clothed Gideon, and sounding the trumpet, he summoned the house of Abiezer to follow him.
verses.6:35: And he sent messengers throughout all Manasseh, which itself also followed him, and other messengers into Asher and Zebulun and Naphtali, and they came to meet him.
verses.6:36: And Gideon said to God, "If You save Israel by my hand, just as You have spoken,
verses.6:37: I will place this fleece of wool on the threshing floor; if dew is on the fleece alone and dryness on all the ground, I will know that by my hand, just as You have spoken, You will deliver Israel."
verses.6:38: And it happened so. And rising in the night, having wrung out the fleece, he filled a bowl with dew.
verses.6:39: And he said again to God, "Do not let Your anger be aroused against me if I test one more time, seeking a sign in the fleece. I pray that the fleece alone may be dry, and all the ground wet with dew."
verses.6:40: And God did on that night as he had requested; and there was dryness on the fleece alone, and dew on all the ground.
verses.7:1: So Jerubbaal, who is also Gideon, rising in the night, and all the people with him, came to the spring that is called Harod. Now the camp of Midian was in the valley on the northern side of the high hill.
verses.7:2: And the Lord said to Gideon, "The people with you are too numerous, and Midian will not be handed over into their hands, so that Israel may not boast against Me and say, 'By my own strength I have been delivered.'
verses.7:3: Speak to the people, and proclaim in the hearing of all, 'Whoever is fearful and timid, let him return.'" And they departed from Mount Gilead, and twenty-two thousand men of the people returned, and only ten thousand remained.
verses.7:4: And the Lord said to Gideon, "The people are still too numerous; lead them to the water, and there I will test them. And the one of whom I say to you that he is to go with you, let him go on; the one whom I forbid to go, let him return."
verses.7:5: And when the people had gone down to the water, the Lord said to Gideon, "Those who lap the water with their tongue, just as dogs are accustomed to lap, you will set them apart by themselves; but those who drink with bent knees will be on the other side."
verses.7:6: So the number of those who lapped the water, tossing it with their hand to their mouth, was three hundred men; but all the rest of the multitude had drunk on bent knee.
verses.7:7: And the Lord said to Gideon, "With the three hundred men who lapped the water I will deliver you, and I will hand Midian over into your hand; but let all the rest of the multitude return to their own place."
verses.7:8: So having taken provisions and trumpets according to their number, he ordered all the rest of the multitude to depart to their tents; and he himself, with the three hundred men, committed himself to the battle. Now the camp of Midian was below in the valley.
verses.7:9: That same night the Lord said to him, "Rise, and go down into the camp, because I have handed them over into your hand.
verses.7:10: But if you are afraid to go alone, let Purah your servant go down with you.
verses.7:11: And when you hear what they are saying, then your hands will be strengthened, and you will go down more confidently to the camp of the enemies." Therefore he himself and Purah his servant went down to the part of the camp where the watches of armed men were.
verses.7:12: Now Midian and Amalek, and all the eastern peoples, lay spread out in the valley like a multitude of locusts; the camels also were innumerable, like the sand that lies on the shore of the sea.
verses.7:13: And when Gideon had come, someone was telling a dream to his companion, and in this manner he was recounting what he had seen: "I saw a dream, and it seemed to me as if a barley loaf baked under the ashes was rolling and coming down into the camp of Midian; and when it had reached the tent, it struck it, and overturned it, and leveled it completely with the ground."
verses.7:14: The one to whom he was speaking answered, "This is nothing other than the sword of Gideon, the son of Joash, an Israelite man; for the Lord has handed over Midian and all its camp into his hands."
verses.7:15: And when Gideon had heard the dream and its interpretation, he worshiped; and he returned to the camp of Israel and said, "Rise, for the Lord has handed over the camp of Midian into our hands."
verses.7:16: And he divided the three hundred men into three divisions, and he put trumpets in their hands, and empty jars, and torches in the middle of the jars.
verses.7:17: And he said to them, "What you see me doing, do that: I will enter a part of the camp, and what I do, follow.
verses.7:18: When the trumpet sounds in my hand, you also blow all around the camp and shout together, 'For the Lord and for Gideon!'"
verses.7:19: And Gideon, and the three hundred men who were with him, entered a part of the camp as the watches of the middle of the night were beginning; and when the guards had been roused, they began to blow the horns and to smash the jars against one another.
verses.7:20: And when they were sounding in three places all around the camp and had shattered the water jars, they held the torches in their left hands and the sounding trumpets in their right hands, and they shouted, "The sword of the Lord and of Gideon!"
verses.7:21: standing each in his own place all around the enemy camp. So the entire camp was thrown into confusion, and shouting and wailing, they fled.
verses.7:22: And nonetheless the three hundred men persisted, sounding the horns. And the Lord sent the sword into the entire camp, and they cut one another down in mutual slaughter,
verses.7:23: fleeing as far as Beth-shittah and the edge of Abel-meholah in Tabbath. Now the men of Israel from Naphtali, and Asher, and all Manasseh, calling out together, pursued Midian.
verses.7:24: And Gideon sent messengers into all the hill country of Ephraim, saying, "Go down to meet Midian, and seize the waters as far as Beth-barah and the Jordan." And all Ephraim called out, and seized the waters and the Jordan beforehand as far as Beth-barah.
verses.7:25: And having captured two men of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb, they killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb, and Zeeb at the winepress of Zeeb. And they pursued Midian, carrying the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon across the streams of the Jordan.
verses.8:1: And the men of Ephraim said to him, "What is this that you wanted to do, that you did not call us when you went to battle against Midian?" quarreling fiercely and nearly inflicting violence.
verses.8:2: He answered them, "For what have I been able to do like what you have done? Is not a grape cluster of Ephraim better than the grape harvests of Abiezer?
verses.8:3: Into your hands the Lord has handed over the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; what have I been able to do like what you have done?" When he had spoken this, their spirit, with which they were swelling against him, subsided.
verses.8:4: And when Gideon had come to the Jordan, he crossed it with the three hundred men who were with him; and because of exhaustion, they were unable to pursue those who were fleeing.
verses.8:5: And he said to the men of Succoth, "Give, I beg you, loaves of bread to the people who are with me, because they have grown very faint, so that we may be able to pursue Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian."
verses.8:6: The princes of Succoth answered, "Perhaps the palms of the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna are in your hand, and for that reason you ask that we give loaves of bread to your army."
verses.8:7: To them he said, "Therefore, when the Lord has handed over Zebah and Zalmunna into my hands, I will crush your flesh with the thorns and thistles of the wilderness."
verses.8:8: And going up from there, he came to Penuel, and he spoke similar things to the men of that place. And they also answered him just as the men of Succoth had answered.
verses.8:9: So he said to them also, "When I have returned as a victor in peace, I will destroy this tower."
verses.8:10: Now Zebah and Zalmunna were resting with all their army. For fifteen thousand men had remained out of all the troops of the eastern peoples, after one hundred twenty thousand warriors drawing the sword had been cut down.
verses.8:11: And Gideon, going up by the way of those who lived in tents on the eastern side of Nobah and Jogbehah, struck the camp of the enemies, who were secure and suspected nothing adverse.
verses.8:12: And Zebah and Zalmunna fled, and Gideon pursued and captured them, after all their army had been thrown into confusion.
verses.8:13: And returning from the war before the rising of the sun,
verses.8:14: he seized a boy from the men of Succoth, and he asked him the names of the princes and elders of Succoth, and he wrote down seventy-seven men.
verses.8:15: And he came to Succoth and said to them, "Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, concerning whom you reproached me, saying, 'Perhaps the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna are in your hands, and for that reason you ask that we give loaves of bread to the men who are weary and have grown faint.'"
verses.8:16: Therefore he took the elders of the city, and thorns and thistles of the wilderness, and with them he crushed and shattered the men of Succoth.
verses.8:17: He also overthrew the tower of Penuel, after killing the inhabitants of the city.
verses.8:18: And he said to Zebah and Zalmunna, "What kind of men were those whom you killed at Tabor?" They answered, "Like you, and one of them was like the son of a king."
verses.8:19: He answered them, "They were my brothers, the sons of my mother. As the Lord lives, if you had spared them, I would not kill you."
verses.8:20: And he said to Jether his firstborn, "Rise, and kill them." But he did not draw his sword, for he was afraid, because he was still a boy.
verses.8:21: And Zebah and Zalmunna said, "Rise yourself, and fall upon us, because a man's strength is according to his age." Gideon rose and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and he took the ornaments and medallions with which the necks of royal camels are accustomed to be adorned.
verses.8:22: And all the men of Israel said to Gideon, "Rule over us, you, and your son, and your son's son, because you have delivered us from the hand of Midian."
verses.8:23: To them he said, "I will not rule over you, nor will my son rule over you, but the Lord will rule over you."
verses.8:24: And he said to them, "I ask one request of you: give me the earrings from your plunder." For the Ishmaelites were accustomed to have golden earrings.
verses.8:25: They answered, "We will most gladly give them." And spreading a cloak upon the ground, they threw onto it the earrings from the plunder.
verses.8:26: And the weight of the requested earrings was one thousand seven hundred shekels of gold, apart from the ornaments, and necklaces, and purple clothing that the kings of Midian were accustomed to use, and besides the golden collars of the camels.
verses.8:27: And Gideon made an ephod out of it and placed it in his city Ophrah. And all Israel prostituted itself with it, and it became a ruin to Gideon and to all his house.
verses.8:28: Now Midian was humbled before the sons of Israel, and they could no longer lift up their necks; but the land had rest for forty years, during which Gideon presided.
verses.8:29: So Jerubbaal, the son of Joash, went away and lived in his own house.
verses.8:30: And he had seventy sons who came out from his thigh, because he had many wives.
verses.8:31: Now his concubine, whom he had in Shechem, bore him a son named Abimelech.
verses.8:32: And Gideon, the son of Joash, died in a good old age, and he was buried in the tomb of Joash his father in Ophrah, of the family of Ezri.
verses.8:33: Now after Gideon died, the sons of Israel turned away and prostituted themselves with the Baals. And they made a covenant with Baal, that he would be a god to them;
verses.8:34: and they did not remember the Lord their God, who rescued them from the hands of all their enemies all around,
verses.8:35: nor did they show mercy to the house of Jerubbaal Gideon, according to all the good things that he had done for Israel.
verses.9:1: Now Abimelech, the son of Jerubbaal, went to Shechem to his mother's brothers and spoke to them and to all the kindred of the house of his mother's father, saying,
verses.9:2: "Speak to all the men of Shechem: 'Which is better for you, that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, have dominion over you, or that one man have dominion? And at the same time consider that I am your bone and your flesh.'"
verses.9:3: And his mother's brothers spoke all these words concerning him to all the men of Shechem, and they inclined their heart after Abimelech, saying, "He is our brother."
verses.9:4: And they gave him seventy pounds of silver from the temple of Baal-berith. With it he hired for himself destitute and wandering men, and they followed him.
verses.9:5: And he came to his father's house in Ophrah and killed his brothers, the sons of Jerubbaal, seventy men, upon one stone; yet Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, remained and was hidden.
verses.9:6: Now all the men of Shechem and all the families of the city of Millo gathered together, and they went and appointed Abimelech as king beside the oak that stood in Shechem.
verses.9:7: When this was reported to Jotham, he went and stood on the summit of Mount Gerizim; and lifting up his voice, he cried out and said, "Listen to me, men of Shechem; so may God listen to you.
verses.9:8: The trees went to anoint a king over themselves, and they said to the olive tree, 'Rule over us.'
verses.9:9: It answered, 'Can I abandon my richness, which both gods and men use, and come to be promoted among the trees?'
verses.9:10: And the trees said to the fig tree, 'Come, and receive the kingdom over us.'
verses.9:11: It answered them, 'Can I abandon my sweetness and most delightful fruits, and go to be promoted among the rest of the trees?'
verses.9:12: And the trees spoke to the vine, 'Come, and rule over us.'
verses.9:13: It answered them, 'Can I abandon my wine, which gladdens God and men, and be promoted among the rest of the trees?'
verses.9:14: And all the trees said to the bramble, 'Come, and rule over us.'
verses.9:15: It answered them, 'If you truly appoint me as king for yourselves, come and rest under my shade; but if you are not willing, let fire come out from the bramble and devour the cedars of Lebanon.'
verses.9:16: Now therefore, if you have rightly and without sin appointed Abimelech as king over yourselves, and have dealt well with Jerubbaal and with his house, and have rendered a return for the benefits of him who fought for you,
verses.9:17: and gave his life over to dangers so that he might rescue you from the hand of Midian,
verses.9:18: you who have now risen up against my father's house, and killed his sons, seventy men, upon one stone, and appointed Abimelech, the son of his female servant, as king over the inhabitants of Shechem, because he is your brother;
verses.9:19: if then you have dealt rightly and without fault with Jerubbaal and his house, rejoice today in Abimelech, and let him rejoice in you.
verses.9:20: But if perversely, let fire come out from him and consume the inhabitants of Shechem and the town of Millo; and let fire come out from the men of Shechem and from the town of Millo and devour Abimelech."
verses.9:21: When he had said these things, he fled and went away to Beer, and he lived there out of fear of his brother Abimelech.
verses.9:22: So Abimelech reigned over Israel for three years.
verses.9:23: And the Lord sent a most evil spirit between Abimelech and the inhabitants of Shechem, who began to detest him
verses.9:24: and to lay the crime of the killing of the seventy sons of Jerubbaal, and the shedding of their blood, upon Abimelech their brother and upon the rest of the rulers of the Shechemites who had helped him.
verses.9:25: And they set ambushes against him on the top of the mountains; and while they waited for his arrival, they practiced robbery, carrying off plunder from those passing by; and it was reported to Abimelech.
verses.9:26: Now Gaal, the son of Obed, came with his brothers and passed over into Shechem. Emboldened at his arrival, the inhabitants of Shechem
verses.9:27: went out into the fields, laying waste the vineyards and treading the grapes; and having formed choirs of singers, they entered the temple of their god, and amid feasts and cups they cursed Abimelech,
verses.9:28: while Gaal, the son of Obed, cried out, "Who is Abimelech, and what is Shechem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jerubbaal, and did he not appoint Zebul his servant as ruler over the men of Hamor, the father of Shechem? Why then will we serve him?
verses.9:29: If only someone would place this people under my hand, so that I might remove Abimelech from the midst!" And it was said to Abimelech, "Gather a multitude of an army, and come."
verses.9:30: For Zebul, the ruler of the city, having heard the words of Gaal, the son of Obed, became very angry,
verses.9:31: and secretly sent messengers to Abimelech, saying, "Look, Gaal, the son of Obed, has come to Shechem with his brothers, and is assailing the city against you.
verses.9:32: Rise up therefore by night with the people who are with you, and lie hidden in the field;
verses.9:33: and early in the morning, as the sun rises, rush upon the city. And when he comes out against you with his people, do to him whatever you can."
verses.9:34: So Abimelech rose up by night with all his army and set ambushes beside Shechem in four places.
verses.9:35: And Gaal, the son of Obed, went out and stood at the entrance of the gate of the city. Then Abimelech, and all the army with him, rose up from the place of ambush.
verses.9:36: And when Gaal saw the people, he said to Zebul, "Look, a multitude is coming down from the mountains." He answered him, "You are seeing the shadows of the mountains like heads of men, and you are deceived by this error."
verses.9:37: And again Gaal said, "Look, people are coming down from the navel of the land, and one column is coming by the road that faces the oak."
verses.9:38: Zebul said to him, "Where is your mouth now, with which you were saying, 'Who is Abimelech, that we should serve him?' Is this not the people whom you despised? Go out and fight against them."
verses.9:39: Therefore Gaal went out, while the people of the Shechemites looked on, and fought against Abimelech,
verses.9:40: who pursued him as he fled and drove him into the city; and very many on his side fell, as far as the gate of the city.
verses.9:41: And Abimelech stayed in Rumah; but Zebul drove Gaal and his companions out of the city and did not allow them to remain in it.
verses.9:42: On the following day, therefore, the people went out into the plain. When this was reported to Abimelech,
verses.9:43: he took his army and divided it into three divisions, setting ambushes in the fields. And seeing that the people were coming out of the city, he rose up and rushed upon them
verses.9:44: with his column, assailing and besieging the city; while the two divisions pursued the adversaries scattered across the plain.
verses.9:45: Moreover, Abimelech assailed the city all that day; and he captured it, having killed its inhabitants and destroyed the city itself, so that he scattered salt in it.
verses.9:46: When those who lived in the tower of the Shechemites heard this, they entered the temple of their god Berith, where they had made a covenant with him, and from it the place had received its name; and it was very strongly fortified.
verses.9:47: Abimelech also, hearing that the men of the tower of the Shechemites were massed together,
verses.9:48: went up Mount Zalmon with all his people; and seizing an axe, he cut off a branch of a tree, and carrying it placed upon his shoulder, he said to his companions, "What you see me doing, do quickly."
verses.9:49: Therefore, eagerly cutting off branches from the trees, they followed their leader. Surrounding the stronghold, they set it on fire; and thus it happened that by smoke and fire a thousand people were killed, men and women alike, of the inhabitants of the tower of Shechem.
verses.9:50: Then Abimelech, setting out from there, came to the town of Thebez, which he surrounded and besieged with his army.
verses.9:51: Now there was a high tower in the middle of the city, to which men and women together, and all the rulers of the city, had fled for refuge, with the door shut very securely, and standing on the roof of the tower along the battlements.
verses.9:52: And Abimelech, coming up beside the tower, fought vigorously; and approaching the doorway, he strove to put fire beneath it;
verses.9:53: and look, one woman, throwing a piece of a millstone from above, dashed it against the head of Abimelech and crushed his brain.
verses.9:54: He quickly called his armor-bearer and said to him, "Unsheathe your sword and strike me, so that it may not perhaps be said that I was killed by a woman." Carrying out the orders, he killed him.
verses.9:55: And when he was dead, all those from Israel who were with him returned to their own dwellings;
verses.9:56: and God repaid the evil that Abimelech had done against his father by killing his seventy brothers.
verses.9:57: What they had done was also repaid to the Shechemites, and the curse of Jotham, the son of Jerubbaal, came upon them.
verses.10:1: After Abimelech, there arose a leader in Israel, Tola the son of Puah, the uncle of Abimelech, a man of Issachar, who lived in Shamir of Mount Ephraim;
verses.10:2: and he judged Israel for twenty-three years, and he died and was buried in Shamir.
verses.10:3: He was succeeded by Jair the Gileadite, who judged Israel for twenty-two years,
verses.10:4: having thirty sons who sat on thirty colts of female donkeys and were chiefs of thirty cities, which have been called Havvoth-jair after his name, that is, the towns of Jair, until the present day, in the land of Gilead.
verses.10:5: And Jair died and was buried in the place whose name is Kamon.
verses.10:6: Now the sons of Israel, adding new sins to the old, did evil in the sight of the Lord and served idols, the Baals and Ashtaroth, and the gods of Syria, and of Sidon, and of Moab, and of the sons of Ammon, and of the Philistines; and they abandoned the Lord and did not worship Him.
verses.10:7: Angry against them, the Lord gave them over into the hands of the Philistines and of the sons of Ammon.
verses.10:8: And they were afflicted and severely oppressed for eighteen years, all who lived across the Jordan in the land of the Amorite, who is in Gilead;
verses.10:9: to such an extent that the sons of Ammon, having crossed the Jordan, devastated Judah and Benjamin and Ephraim; and Israel was exceedingly afflicted.
verses.10:10: And crying out to the Lord, they said, "We have sinned against You, because we have abandoned the Lord our God and served the Baals."
verses.10:11: The Lord spoke to them, "Did not the Egyptians and the Amorites, and the sons of Ammon and the Philistines,
verses.10:12: the Sidonians also, and Amalek, and Canaan oppress you, and you cried out to Me, and I rescued you from their hand?
verses.10:13: And yet you have abandoned Me and worshiped foreign gods; therefore I will not continue to deliver you any longer:
verses.10:14: go and call upon the gods whom you have chosen; let them deliver you in the time of distress."
verses.10:15: And the sons of Israel said to the Lord, "We have sinned; render to us whatever pleases You, only deliver us now."
verses.10:16: Saying these things, they cast out all the idols of foreign gods from their borders and served the Lord God, who grieved over their miseries.
verses.10:17: Therefore the sons of Ammon, crying out together, pitched their tents in Gilead; and against them the sons of Israel gathered together and encamped in Mizpah.
verses.10:18: And the chiefs of Gilead said, each one to his neighbors, "Whoever among us first begins to fight against the sons of Ammon will be the leader of the people of Gilead."
verses.11:1: At that time there was Jephthah the Gileadite, a very mighty man and a warrior, the son of a woman who was a prostitute, who was born of Gilead.
verses.11:2: Now Gilead had a wife by whom he had sons; and after they had grown up, they drove out Jephthah, saying, "You will not be able to be an heir in our father's house, because you were born of another mother."
verses.11:3: Fleeing from them and avoiding them, he lived in the land of Tob; and men who were destitute and practiced banditry gathered to him, and they followed him as a chief.
verses.11:4: In those days the sons of Ammon were fighting against Israel.
verses.11:5: While they were pressing fiercely, the elders of Gilead set out to bring Jephthah from the land of Tob to their aid;
verses.11:6: and they said to him, "Come and be our chief, and fight against the sons of Ammon."
verses.11:7: He answered them, "Are you not the ones who hated me and drove me out of my father's house? And now you have come to me, driven by necessity."
verses.11:8: And the chiefs of Gilead said to Jephthah, "For this reason, therefore, we have now come to you, so that you may set out with us and fight against the sons of Ammon, and be the leader of all who live in Gilead."
verses.11:9: Jephthah also said to them, "If you have truly come to me so that I may fight for you against the sons of Ammon, and the Lord gives them over into my hands, will I be your chief?"
verses.11:10: They answered him, "The Lord, who hears these things, He Himself is mediator and witness that we will carry out our promises."
verses.11:11: So Jephthah went with the chiefs of Gilead, and all the people made him their chief. And Jephthah spoke all his words before the Lord in Mizpah.
verses.11:12: And he sent messengers to the king of the sons of Ammon to say on his behalf, "What is there between me and you, that you have come against me to devastate my land?"
verses.11:13: He answered them, "Because Israel took my land when he went up from Egypt, from the borders of the Arnon as far as the Jabbok and the Jordan; now, therefore, return it to me in peace."
verses.11:14: Through them Jephthah sent word again and commanded them to say to the king of Ammon,
verses.11:15: "This is what Jephthah says: Israel did not take the land of Moab, nor the land of the sons of Ammon;
verses.11:16: but when they went up from Egypt, he walked through the wilderness as far as the Red Sea and came to Kadesh.
verses.11:17: And he sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, 'Let me pass through your land.' Yet he refused to yield to his pleas. He also sent to the king of Moab, who likewise disdained to grant passage. Therefore he remained in Kadesh,
verses.11:18: and went around along the side of the land of Edom and the land of Moab, and came opposite the eastern region of the land of Moab, and encamped across the Arnon; nor did he wish to enter the territory of Moab. (For the Arnon is the boundary of the land of Moab.)
verses.11:19: So Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and they said to him, 'Let me pass through your land as far as the river.'
verses.11:20: He too, despising the words of Israel, did not allow him to pass through his territory; instead, having gathered a countless multitude, he went out against him at Jahaz and resisted vigorously.
verses.11:21: And the Lord gave him over, together with all his army, into the hands of Israel, who struck him down and possessed all the land of the Amorite, the inhabitant of that region,
verses.11:22: and all its borders, from the Arnon as far as the Jabbok, and from the wilderness as far as the Jordan.
verses.11:23: Therefore the Lord, the God of Israel, overthrew the Amorite while His people Israel fought against him, and do you now want to possess his land?
verses.11:24: Are not the things that Chemosh your god possesses owed to you by right? Yet the things that the Lord our God has obtained as victor will pass into our possession;
verses.11:25: unless perhaps you are better than Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, or can prove that he contended against Israel and fought against him,
verses.11:26: when he lived in Heshbon and its villages, and in Aroer and its settlements, or in all the cities beside the Jordan, for three hundred years. Why in so long a time did you attempt nothing regarding this claim?
verses.11:27: Therefore I am not sinning against you, but you are acting wrongly against me, declaring unjust wars on me. May the Lord, the arbiter of this day, judge between Israel and the sons of Ammon."
verses.11:28: And the king of the sons of Ammon refused to yield to the words of Jephthah, which he had sent through the messengers.
verses.11:29: Therefore the Spirit of the Lord came upon Jephthah, and going around Gilead and Manasseh, and also Mizpah of Gilead, and crossing over from there to the sons of Ammon,
verses.11:30: he vowed a vow to the Lord, saying, "If You give the sons of Ammon over into my hands,
verses.11:31: whoever first comes out of the doors of my house and meets me as I return in peace from the sons of Ammon, him I will offer as a burnt offering to the Lord."
verses.11:32: And Jephthah crossed over to the sons of Ammon to fight against them, whom the Lord gave over into his hands.
verses.11:33: And he struck from Aroer until you come to Minnith, twenty cities, and as far as Abel, which is planted with vineyards, with a very great blow; and the sons of Ammon were humbled by the sons of Israel.
verses.11:34: Now as Jephthah was returning to Mizpah, to his house, his only-born daughter met him with tambourines and dances; for he had no other children.
verses.11:35: When he saw her, he tore his garments and said, "Alas for me, my daughter! You have deceived me, and you yourself have been deceived; for I have opened my mouth to the Lord, and I will not be able to do otherwise."
verses.11:36: She answered him, "My father, if you have opened your mouth to the Lord, do to me whatever you have promised, since vengeance and victory over your enemies have been granted to you."
verses.11:37: And she said to her father, "Grant me this one thing that I ask: let me go so that for two months I may go around the mountains and mourn my virginity with my companions."
verses.11:38: He answered her, "Go." And he let her go for two months. And when she had gone away with her friends and companions, she wept over her virginity in the mountains.
verses.11:39: And when the two months were completed, she returned to her father, and he did to her just as he had vowed, she who did not know a man. From then on a custom became widespread in Israel, and a practice was kept,
verses.11:40: that after the cycle of a year the daughters of Israel gather together and mourn the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite for four days.
verses.12:1: Now an uprising arose in Ephraim; for, crossing over toward the north, they said to Jephthah, "Why, when going to battle against the sons of Ammon, were you unwilling to call us so that we might go with you? Therefore we will burn your house."
verses.12:2: He answered them, "I and my people had a fierce dispute against the sons of Ammon, and I called you so that you might provide me help, and you were unwilling to do so.
verses.12:3: Seeing this, I put my life in my hands and crossed over to the sons of Ammon, and the Lord handed them over into my hands. What have I deserved, that you rise up against me in battle?"
verses.12:4: Therefore, having called all the men of Gilead to himself, he fought against Ephraim; and the men of Gilead struck down Ephraim, because Ephraim had said, "Gilead is a fugitive from Ephraim and lives in the midst of Ephraim and Manasseh."
verses.12:5: And the Gileadites seized the fords of the Jordan, by which Ephraim was about to return. And whenever one from the number of Ephraim came to them, fleeing, and said, "I beg you to permit me to cross over," the Gileadites would say to him, "Are you an Ephraimite?" And when he said, "I am not,"
verses.12:6: they would ask him, "Then say Shibboleth," which means "ear of grain." And he would answer, "Sibboleth," not being able to pronounce "ear of grain" with the same letter. And immediately seizing him, they would slaughter him at the very crossing of the Jordan. And forty-two thousand from Ephraim fell at that time.
verses.12:7: So Jephthah the Gileadite judged Israel for six years; and he died and was buried in his city, Gilead.
verses.12:8: After him, Ibzan of Bethlehem judged Israel,
verses.12:9: who had thirty sons and just as many daughters, whom he sent abroad and gave to husbands, and he took the same number of wives for his sons, bringing them into his house. And he judged Israel for seven years,
verses.12:10: and he died and was buried in Bethlehem.
verses.12:11: Aijalon the Zebulunite succeeded him, and he judged Israel for ten years,
verses.12:12: and he died and was buried in Zebulun.
verses.12:13: After him, Abdon the son of Hillel, the Pirathonite, judged Israel,
verses.12:14: who had forty sons and thirty grandsons from them, riding on seventy colts of female donkeys. And he judged Israel for eight years,
verses.12:15: and he died and was buried in Pirathon of the land of Ephraim, on Mount Amalek.
verses.13:1: And again the sons of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, who handed them over into the hands of the Philistines for forty years.
verses.13:2: Now there was a certain man of Zorah, and of the lineage of Dan, named Manoah, having a barren wife.
verses.13:3: The angel of the Lord appeared to her and said to her, "You are barren and without children, but you will conceive and bear a son.
verses.13:4: Be careful, therefore, not to drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean,
verses.13:5: for you will conceive and bear a son, whose head no razor will touch; for he will be a Nazirite of God from his infancy and from his mother's womb, and he himself will begin to deliver Israel from the hand of the Philistines."
verses.13:6: When she came to her husband, she said to him, "A man of God came to me, having an angelic appearance, exceedingly terrifying. When I asked him who he was, and where he had come from, and by what name he was called, he was unwilling to tell me,
verses.13:7: but he answered this: 'Look, you will conceive and bear a son; be careful not to drink wine or strong drink, and not to eat anything unclean, for the boy will be a Nazirite of God from his infancy, from his mother's womb until the day of his death.'"
verses.13:8: So Manoah prayed to the Lord and said, "I implore You, Lord, that the man of God whom You sent may come again and teach us what we ought to do concerning the boy who is about to be born."
verses.13:9: And the Lord heard Manoah as he pleaded, and the angel of God appeared again to his wife as she was sitting in the field; but Manoah her husband was not with her. And when she saw the angel,
verses.13:10: she hurried and ran to her husband, and told him, saying, "Look, the man whom I had seen before has appeared to me."
verses.13:11: And he arose and followed his wife; and coming to the man, he said to him, "Are you the one who spoke to the woman?" And he answered, "I am."
verses.13:12: Manoah said to him, "When your word has been fulfilled, what do you want the boy to do? Or from what will he have to guard himself?"
verses.13:13: And the angel of the Lord said to Manoah, "Let her abstain from all that I spoke of to your wife,
verses.13:14: and let her not eat whatever grows from the vine; let her not drink wine or strong drink; let her eat nothing unclean; and let her fulfill and keep what I commanded her."
verses.13:15: And Manoah said to the angel of the Lord, "I beg you to consent to my requests, and let us prepare for you a young goat from the goats."
verses.13:16: The angel answered him, "If you compel me, I will not eat your bread; but if you want to make a burnt offering, offer it to the Lord." And Manoah did not know that he was the angel of the Lord.
verses.13:17: And he said to him, "What is your name, so that, if your word has been fulfilled, we may honor you?"
verses.13:18: He answered him, "Why do you ask my name, which is wonderful?"
verses.13:19: So Manoah took a young goat from the goats and drink offerings, and placed them on the rock, offering them to the Lord, who performs wonders; and he himself and his wife were looking on.
verses.13:20: And as the flame of the altar ascended into heaven, the angel of the Lord likewise ascended in the flame. When Manoah and his wife saw this, they fell face down to the ground,
verses.13:21: and the angel of the Lord no longer appeared to them. And immediately Manoah realized that he was the angel of the Lord,
verses.13:22: and he said to his wife, "We will certainly die, because we have seen God."
verses.13:23: The woman answered him, "If the Lord wanted to kill us, He would not have accepted a burnt offering and drink offerings from our hands, nor would He have shown us all these things, nor would He have told us the things that are to come."
verses.13:24: So she bore a son and called his name Samson. And the boy grew, and the Lord blessed him.
verses.13:25: And the Spirit of the Lord began to be with him in the camp of Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.
verses.14:1: Then Samson went down to Timnah; and seeing a woman there from the daughters of the Philistines,
verses.14:2: he went up and told his father and his mother, saying, "I saw a woman in Timnah from the daughters of the Philistines; I ask that you take her for me as a wife."
verses.14:3: His father and his mother said to him, "Is there not a woman among the daughters of your brothers, and among all my people, that you want to take a wife from the Philistines, who are uncircumcised?" And Samson said to his father, "Take this one for me, because she has pleased my eyes."
verses.14:4: Now his parents did not know that the matter was coming about from the Lord, and that he was seeking an occasion against the Philistines; for at that time the Philistines were ruling over Israel.
verses.14:5: So Samson went down with his father and mother to Timnah. And when they came to the vineyards of the town, a fierce and roaring young lion appeared and came to meet him.
verses.14:6: Then the Spirit of the Lord rushed upon Samson, and he tore the lion apart, as though ripping a young goat into pieces, having nothing at all in his hand; and he was unwilling to reveal this to his father and mother.
verses.14:7: And he went down and spoke to the woman who had pleased his eyes.
verses.14:8: And after some days, returning to take her, he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion, and look, a swarm of bees was in the mouth of the lion, and a honeycomb.
verses.14:9: When he had taken it in his hands, he ate along the way; and coming to his father and mother, he gave them a portion, and they themselves also ate; yet he did not want to reveal to them that he had taken the honey from the body of the lion.
verses.14:10: So his father went down to the woman, and he made a feast for his son Samson, for young men were accustomed to do so.
verses.14:11: Then, when the townspeople of that place saw him, they gave him thirty companions to be with him.
verses.14:12: Samson spoke to them, "I will propose a riddle to you; if you solve it for me within the seven days of the feast, I will give you thirty linen garments and just as many tunics;
verses.14:13: but if you are not able to solve it, you will give me thirty linen garments and the same number of tunics." And they answered him, "Propose the riddle, so that we may hear it."
verses.14:14: And he said to them, "From the eater came food, and from the strong came sweetness." And for three days they were not able to solve the riddle.
verses.14:15: And when the seventh day arrived, they said to Samson's wife, "Coax your husband and persuade him to reveal to you what the riddle means; but if you are unwilling to do this, we will burn you and your father's house. Or did you invite us to the wedding for this reason, so that you might plunder us?"
verses.14:16: And she poured out tears before Samson and complained, saying, "You hate me and do not love me; for that reason you do not want to explain to me the riddle that you proposed to the sons of my people." But he answered, "I was unwilling to tell my father and mother, and will I be able to reveal it to you?"
verses.14:17: Therefore, during the seven days of the feast she wept before him; and at last on the seventh day, because she was troubling him, he explained it. And she immediately revealed it to her townspeople.
verses.14:18: And they said to him on the seventh day before sunset, "What is sweeter than honey, and what is stronger than a lion?" And he said to them, "If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have found out my riddle."
verses.14:19: Then the Spirit of the Lord rushed upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon and struck down thirty men there, whose garments he took and gave to those who had solved the riddle. And exceedingly angry, he went up to his father's house,
verses.14:20: but his wife took as a husband one of his friends and groomsmen.
verses.15:1: Now after a short time, when the days of the wheat harvest were at hand, Samson came, wanting to visit his wife, and he brought her a young goat from the goats. And when he wanted to enter her inner room as usual, her father stopped him, saying,
verses.15:2: "I thought that you hated her, and therefore I gave her to your friend; but she has a sister who is younger and more beautiful than she is. Let her be a wife for you in her place."
verses.15:3: Samson answered him, "From this day there will be no blame on me against the Philistines, for I will do harm to you."
verses.15:4: And he went and caught three hundred foxes, and joined their tails tail to tail, and bound torches in the middle.
verses.15:5: Setting the torches on fire, he let the foxes go so that they would run here and there. They immediately went into the grainfields of the Philistines. When these were set on fire, both the crops already gathered and those still standing on the stalk were burned up, to such an extent that the flame consumed the vineyards and olive groves as well.
verses.15:6: And the Philistines said, "Who did this thing?" It was said to them, "Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite; because he took his wife and gave her to another, he has done these things." And the Philistines went up and burned both the woman and her father.
verses.15:7: Samson said to them, "Even though you have done these things, yet I will still exact vengeance from you, and then I will rest."
verses.15:8: And he struck them with a great blow, so that, stunned, they placed calf upon thigh. And going down, he lived in the cave of the rock of Etam.
verses.15:9: Therefore the Philistines, going up into the land of Judah, encamped in the place that afterward was called Lehi, that is, Jawbone, where their army was spread out.
verses.15:10: And those from the tribe of Judah said to them, "Why have you come up against us?" They answered, "We have come to bind Samson and to repay him what he has done against us."
verses.15:11: Therefore three thousand men of Judah went down to the cavern of the crag of Etam, and they said to Samson, "Do you not know that the Philistines rule over us? Why did you want to do this?" He said to them, "Just as they did to me, so I did to them."
verses.15:12: "We have come," they said, "to bind you and to hand you over into the hands of the Philistines." Samson said to them, "Swear and pledge to me that you will not kill me."
verses.15:13: They said, "We will not kill you, but we will hand you over bound." And they bound him with two new ropes and brought him from the rock of Etam.
verses.15:14: When he had come to the place of the Jawbone, and the Philistines had come shouting to meet him, the Spirit of the Lord rushed upon him; and just as flax is accustomed to be consumed at the scent of fire, so the bonds with which he had been bound were broken apart and loosened.
verses.15:15: And finding a jawbone, that is, the lower jaw of a donkey, which was lying there, he seized it and killed a thousand men with it.
verses.15:16: And he said, "With the jawbone of a donkey, with the lower jaw of the colt of female donkeys, I have destroyed them and struck a thousand men."
verses.15:17: And when he had finished singing these words, he threw the lower jaw from his hand, and he called the name of that place Ramath-lehi, which is interpreted, Lifting Up of the Jawbone.
verses.15:18: And being very thirsty, he cried out to the Lord and said, "You have given into the hand of Your servant this very great deliverance and victory; look, I am dying of thirst, and I will fall into the hands of the uncircumcised."
verses.15:19: Therefore the Lord opened a molar tooth in the jawbone of the donkey, and waters came out from it. Having drunk them, he refreshed his spirit and recovered his strength. For that reason the name of that place was called Spring of the One Calling from the Jawbone, until the present day.
verses.15:20: And he judged Israel in the days of the Philistines for twenty years.
verses.16:1: He also went to Gaza, and saw there a woman who was a prostitute, and he went in to her.
verses.16:2: When the Philistines had heard this, and it had spread widely among them that Samson had entered the city, they surrounded him, stationing guards at the gate of the city and waiting there all night in silence, so that when morning came they might kill him as he went out.
verses.16:3: Now Samson slept until midnight; and rising up from there, he seized both doors of the gate with their posts and bar, and placing them on his shoulders, he carried them to the top of the mountain that faces Hebron.
verses.16:4: After these things he loved a woman who lived in the valley of Sorek and was called Delilah.
verses.16:5: And the rulers of the Philistines came to her and said, "Deceive him, and learn from him in what he has such great strength, and how we may be able to overcome him and afflict him when bound; and if you do this, we will each give you one thousand one hundred pieces of silver."
verses.16:6: Therefore Delilah spoke to Samson, "Tell me, please, in what your greatest strength lies, and what it is with which, being bound, you cannot break free?"
verses.16:7: Samson answered her, "If I am bound with seven sinew cords not yet dry and still moist, I will be weak like other men."
verses.16:8: And the satraps of the Philistines brought to her seven cords, as he had said, with which she bound him.
verses.16:9: While an ambush was hiding with her and waiting in the inner room for the outcome of the matter, she cried out to him, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" And he broke the bonds, just as if someone were to break a thread twisted from the refuse of tow when it has caught the scent of fire; and it was not known in what his strength lay.
verses.16:10: And Delilah said to him, "Look, you have mocked me and spoken falsely; at least now tell me with what you should be bound."
verses.16:11: He answered her, "If I am bound with new ropes that have never been in use, I will be weak and like other men."
verses.16:12: With these Delilah bound him again and cried out, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" with an ambush prepared in the inner room. And he broke the bonds as though they were threads of webs.
verses.16:13: And Delilah said to him again, "How long will you deceive me and speak falsely? Show me with what you should be bound." Samson answered her, "If you weave the seven locks of my head with the warp, and drive a peg wrapped with them into the ground, I will be weak."
verses.16:14: When Delilah had done this, she said to him, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" And rising up from sleep, he pulled out the peg with the locks and the warp.
verses.16:15: And Delilah said to him, "How do you say that you love me, when your mind is not with me? Three times you have lied to me, and you have not been willing to say in what your greatest strength lies."
verses.16:16: And when she was troublesome to him and continually pressed upon him for many days, giving no space for rest, his soul fainted and was wearied even to death.
verses.16:17: Then, revealing the truth of the matter, he said to her, "Iron has never come upon my head, because I am a Nazirite, that is, consecrated to God, from my mother's womb. If my head is shaved, my strength will depart from me, and I will grow faint, and I will be like other men."
verses.16:18: And seeing that he had confessed to her his whole mind, she sent to the rulers of the Philistines and sent word, "Come up once more, because now he has opened his heart to me." And they came up, taking the money that they had promised.
verses.16:19: And she made him sleep upon her knees and rest his head in her lap. And she called a barber and shaved his seven locks, and she began to drive him away and push him back from herself, for immediately strength departed from him.
verses.16:20: And she said, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" And rising up from sleep, he said in his mind, "I will go out as I did before and shake myself free," not knowing that the Lord had departed from him.
verses.16:21: When the Philistines had seized him, they immediately gouged out his eyes and led him to Gaza bound with chains; and having shut him up in prison, they made him grind.
verses.16:22: And already his hair began to grow back.
verses.16:23: And the rulers of the Philistines gathered together to offer magnificent sacrifices to Dagon their god and to feast, saying, "Our god has handed over our enemy Samson into our hands."
verses.16:24: Seeing this as well, the people praised their god and said the same things, "Our god has handed over our adversary into our hands, who destroyed our land and killed very many."
verses.16:25: And rejoicing throughout the banquets, having already partaken of the feast, they commanded that Samson be called and play before them. Brought from the prison, he played before them, and they made him stand between two pillars.
verses.16:26: And he said to the boy guiding his steps, "Let go of me, so that I may touch the pillars on which the whole house rests, and lean upon them, and rest a little."
verses.16:27: Now the house was full of men and women, and all the rulers of the Philistines were there, and from the roof and terrace about three thousand of both sexes were watching Samson play.
verses.16:28: But having called upon the Lord, he said, "Lord God, remember me, and restore to me now my former strength, my God, that I may avenge myself on my enemies, and for the loss of my two eyes may receive one vengeance."
verses.16:29: And seizing both pillars on which the house rested, and holding one of them with his right hand and the other with his left,
