verses.16:30: he said, "Let my soul die with the Philistines." And when he had forcefully shaken the pillars, the house fell upon all the rulers and the rest of the multitude that was there; and dying, he killed many more than he had killed before while alive.
verses.16:31: Now his brothers and his entire clan went down, took his body, and buried it between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of his father Manoah. And he judged Israel for twenty years.
verses.17:1: There was at that time a certain man from Mount Ephraim named Micah,
verses.17:2: who said to his mother, "The one thousand one hundred pieces of silver that you had set apart for yourself, and over which you had sworn in my hearing, look, I have them, and they are with me." She answered him, "Blessed be my son by the Lord."
verses.17:3: Therefore he returned them to his mother, who had said to him, "I have consecrated and vowed this silver to the Lord, that my son may receive it from my hand and make a carved image and a cast image; and now I hand it over to you."
verses.17:4: So he returned them to his mother; and she took two hundred pieces of silver and gave them to a silversmith, so that he would make from them a carved image and a cast image, which was in the house of Micah.
verses.17:5: He also set apart in it a small shrine for a god, and he made an ephod and teraphim, that is, a priestly garment and idols; and he filled the hand of one of his sons, and he became a priest for him.
verses.17:6: In those days there was no king in Israel, but each one did what seemed right to himself.
verses.17:7: There was also another young man from Bethlehem of Judah, from its clan; and he himself was a Levite, and he lived there.
verses.17:8: And going out from the city of Bethlehem, he wanted to sojourn wherever he might find it suitable for himself. And when he had come into Mount Ephraim while making his journey, and had turned aside briefly into the house of Micah,
verses.17:9: he was asked by him where he had come from. He answered, "I am a Levite from Bethlehem of Judah, and I am going to live where I am able and perceive it to be useful for me."
verses.17:10: And Micah said, "Stay with me, and be a father and a priest to me; and I will give you ten pieces of silver each year, and a double garment, and the things that are necessary for sustenance."
verses.17:11: He agreed and stayed with the man, and he was to him like one of his sons.
verses.17:12: And Micah filled his hand, and he had the youth as a priest with him,
verses.17:13: saying, "Now I know that God will do good to me, since I have a priest of the Levitical lineage."
verses.18:1: In those days there was no king in Israel, and the tribe of Dan was seeking a possession for itself so that it might live in it; for up to that day it had not received an allotment among the other tribes.
verses.18:2: Therefore the sons of Dan sent five very valiant men of their lineage and family from Zorah and Eshtaol to scout out the land and inspect it carefully, and they said to them, "Go and examine the land." When they went on and came to Mount Ephraim, and entered the house of Micah, they rested there.
verses.18:3: And recognizing the voice of the young Levite, and making use of his lodging, they said to him, "Who brings you here? What are you doing here? For what reason did you want to come here?"
verses.18:4: He answered them, "Micah has done such and such things for me, and he has hired me for wages so that I may be a priest to him."
verses.18:5: Then they asked him to consult the Lord, so that they might know whether they were proceeding on a prosperous journey and the matter would have success.
verses.18:6: He answered them, "Go in peace; the Lord looks upon your way, and the journey on which you are going."
verses.18:7: So the five men went and came to Laish, and they saw the people living in it without any fear, according to the custom of the Sidonians, secure and quiet, with no one resisting them at all, and of great wealth, and far from Sidon and separated from all men.
verses.18:8: And returning to their brothers in Zorah and Eshtaol, they answered those who asked what they had done,
verses.18:9: "Rise up, let us go up against them; for we have seen a very rich and fertile land. Do not be negligent, do not delay; let us go and possess it; there will be no toil.
verses.18:10: We will enter among a secure people, into a very broad region, and the Lord will deliver to us a place in which there is no lack of any of the things that are produced on the earth."
verses.18:11: So six hundred men set out from the clan of Dan, that is, from Zorah and Eshtaol, girded with battle weapons.
verses.18:12: And going up, they stayed in Kiriath-jearim of Judah; from that time that place received the name Camp of Dan, and it is behind Kiriath-jearim.
verses.18:13: From there they passed into Mount Ephraim. And when they came to the house of Micah,
verses.18:14: the five men who had previously been sent to examine the land of Laish said to the rest of their brothers, "Do you know that in these houses there is an ephod, and teraphim, and a carved image, and a cast image? See what pleases you."
verses.18:15: And when they had turned aside a little, they entered the house of the young Levite, who was in the house of Micah, and they greeted him with peaceful words.
verses.18:16: Meanwhile, the six hundred men, armed just as they were, stood before the door.
verses.18:17: But those who had entered the house of the young man were trying to take the carved image, and the ephod, and the teraphim, and the cast image, and the priest was standing before the door, with the six hundred very valiant men waiting not far off.
verses.18:18: Therefore those who had gone in took the carved image, the ephod, and the idols, and the cast image. The priest said to them, "What are you doing?"
verses.18:19: They answered him, "Be silent and put your finger over your mouth, and come with us so that we may have you as a father and a priest. What is better for you: to be a priest in the house of one man, or in one tribe and family in Israel?"
verses.18:20: When he heard this, he consented to their words, and he took the ephod, and the idols, and the carved image, and set out with them.
verses.18:21: As they went on, and had made the little ones and the livestock and everything that was valuable go ahead of them,
verses.18:22: and were already far from the house of Micah, the men who lived in the houses of Micah shouted out together and pursued them,
verses.18:23: and began to shout from behind. When they looked back, they said to Micah, "What do you want? Why are you shouting?"
verses.18:24: He answered, "You have taken my gods, which I made for myself, and the priest, and everything that I have, and you say, 'What is the matter with you?'"
verses.18:25: And the sons of Dan said to him, "Watch out that you do not speak to us any further, or men provoked in spirit will come upon you, and you yourself with your entire household will perish."
verses.18:26: And so they went on with the journey they had begun. And Micah, seeing that they were stronger than he was, returned to his own house.
verses.18:27: Now the six hundred men took the priest and the things we mentioned above, and they came to Laish, to a quiet and secure people, and struck them with the edge of the sword, and gave the city over to fire,
verses.18:28: with no one at all bringing aid, because they lived far from Sidon and had no fellowship or dealings of any kind with any man. Now the city was situated in the region of Rehob; and rebuilding it, they lived in it,
verses.18:29: calling the name of the city Dan, after the name of their father whom Israel had fathered; previously it was called Laish.
verses.18:30: And they set up the carved image for themselves, and appointed Jonathan son of Gershom, son of Moses, and his sons as priests in the tribe of Dan until the day of their captivity.
verses.18:31: And the idol of Micah remained with them all the time that the house of God was in Shiloh. In those days there was no king in Israel.
verses.19:1: There was a certain Levite man living on the side of Mount Ephraim, who took a wife from Bethlehem of Judah,
verses.19:2: who left him and returned to her father's house in Bethlehem, and stayed with him for four months.
verses.19:3: And her husband followed her, wanting to be reconciled to her, and to speak tenderly to her, and to bring her back with him, having in his company a servant and two donkeys; and she received him and brought him into her father's house. When his father-in-law heard this and saw him, he went to meet him joyfully,
verses.19:4: and embraced the man. And the son-in-law stayed in the house of his father-in-law for three days, eating and drinking with him on friendly terms.
verses.19:5: On the fourth day, rising while it was still night, he wanted to set out; but his father-in-law detained him and said to him, "First taste a little bit of bread and strengthen your stomach, and then you will set out."
verses.19:6: And they sat down together, and ate and drank. And the father of the young woman said to his son-in-law, "I urge you to stay here today, and let us rejoice together."
verses.19:7: But rising up, he began wanting to set out. And nevertheless his father-in-law earnestly detained him and made him stay with him.
verses.19:8: When morning came, the Levite was preparing for the journey. "I ask you," his father-in-law said to him again, "to take a little food, and having regained strength until the day advances, to set out afterward." So they ate together.
verses.19:9: And the young man rose up to go on his way with his wife and servant. His father-in-law spoke to him again, "Consider that the day is declining further toward sunset and is drawing near to evening; stay with me today also and spend a joyful day, and tomorrow you will set out to go to your own house."
verses.19:10: The son-in-law would not consent to his words, but went on immediately and came opposite Jebus, which by another name is called Jerusalem, leading with him two loaded donkeys and the concubine.
verses.19:11: And now they were near Jebus, and the day was turning into night; and the servant said to his master, "Come, I implore you, let us turn aside to the city of the Jebusites and stay in it."
verses.19:12: His master answered him, "I will not enter a town of a foreign nation, which is not of the sons of Israel, but I will pass on as far as Gibeah,
verses.19:13: and when I arrive there, we will stay in it, or at least in the city of Ramah."
verses.19:14: So they passed by Jebus and continued on the journey they had begun, and the sun set on them near Gibeah, which is in the tribe of Benjamin.
verses.19:15: And they turned aside to it to stay there. When they had entered it, they sat in the square of the city, and no one was willing to receive them for lodging.
verses.19:16: And look, an old man appeared, returning from the field and from his work in the evening, who himself was also from Mount Ephraim and was living as a foreigner in Gibeah; but the men of that region were sons of Jemini.
verses.19:17: And lifting up his eyes, the old man saw the man sitting with his small bundles in the square of the city, and he said to him, "Where are you coming from, and where are you going?"
verses.19:18: He answered him, "We have set out from Bethlehem of Judah, and we are going to our own place, which is on the side of Mount Ephraim, from where we had gone to Bethlehem; and now we are going to the house of God, and no one is willing to receive us under his roof,
verses.19:19: though we have straw and hay for fodder for the donkeys, and bread and wine for my use and that of your maidservant, and of the servant who is with me; we need nothing except lodging."
verses.19:20: The old man answered him, "Peace be with you; I will provide everything that is necessary; only, please, do not stay in the square."
verses.19:21: And he brought him into his house and provided fodder for the donkeys; and after they washed their feet, he received them to a feast.
verses.19:22: While they were feasting and refreshing their bodies with food and drink after the toil of the journey, the men of that city came, sons of Belial (that is, without a yoke), and surrounding the old man's house, they began to pound on the doors, shouting to the master of the house and saying, "Bring out the man who entered your house, so that we may abuse him."
verses.19:23: And the old man went out to them and said, "No, brothers, do not do this evil, because the man has entered my lodging; and cease from this folly.
verses.19:24: I have a virgin daughter, and this man has a concubine; I will bring them out to you so that you may humble them and satisfy your lust; only, I implore you, do not commit this crime against nature upon the man."
verses.19:25: They would not consent to his words; seeing this, the man brought his concubine out to them and handed her over to them to be violated; and after they had abused her all night, they let her go in the morning.
verses.19:26: But the woman, as the darkness was receding, came to the door of the house where her master was staying, and collapsed there.
verses.19:27: When morning came, the man rose up and opened the door to complete the journey he had begun; and look, his concubine was lying before the door with her hands spread out on the threshold.
verses.19:28: Thinking she was resting, he spoke to her, "Rise up, and let us go." When she answered nothing, realizing that she was dead, he took her and placed her on the donkey, and returned to his own house.
verses.19:29: When he had entered it, he seized a sword, and cutting the corpse of his wife, together with her bones, into twelve parts and pieces, he sent them into all the territories of Israel.
verses.19:30: When each one saw this, they cried out together, "Never has such a thing been done in Israel, from the day on which our fathers came up out of Egypt until the present time; render a judgment, and decide in common what needs to be done."
verses.20:1: Therefore all the sons of Israel went out and were gathered together as one man, from Dan to Beersheba and the land of Gilead, to the Lord in Mizpah.
verses.20:2: And all the corners of the peoples, and all the tribes of Israel, came together into the assembly of the people of God, four hundred thousand fighting foot soldiers.
verses.20:3: (And it was not hidden from the sons of Benjamin that the sons of Israel had gone up to Mizpah.) And when the Levite, the husband of the murdered woman, was asked how so great a crime had been committed,
verses.20:4: he answered, "I came to Gibeah of Benjamin with my wife and turned in there,
verses.20:5: and look, at night the men of that city surrounded the house in which I was staying, wanting to kill me and abusing my wife with an unbelievable frenzy of lust; finally she died.
verses.20:6: I took hold of her, cut her into pieces, and sent the parts into all the borders of your possession, because never has so great a wickedness and so heinous a sin been done in Israel.
verses.20:7: You are present, all you sons of Israel; decide what you ought to do."
verses.20:8: And all the people stood and answered as with the speech of one man, "We will not withdraw to our tents, nor will anyone enter his own house;
verses.20:9: but let us do this in common against Gibeah.
verses.20:10: Let ten men be chosen out of a hundred from all the tribes of Israel, and a hundred out of a thousand, and a thousand out of ten thousand, so that they may bring provisions for the army, and we may be able to fight against Gibeah of Benjamin and repay it what it deserves for the crime."
verses.20:11: And all Israel came together to the city as one man, with the same mind and one counsel.
verses.20:12: And they sent messengers to the whole tribe of Benjamin to say, "Why has so great a wickedness been found among you?
verses.20:13: Hand over the men of Gibeah who committed this outrage, so that they may die and evil may be taken away from Israel." But they were unwilling to listen to the command of their brothers, the sons of Israel;
verses.20:14: instead, from all the cities that belonged to their lot, they came together to Gibeah to bring them help and to fight against the entire people of Israel.
verses.20:15: And twenty-five thousand from Benjamin who drew the sword were found, besides the inhabitants of Gibeah,
verses.20:16: who were seven hundred very valiant men, fighting with the left hand just as with the right, and hurling stones with slings so accurately that they could strike even a hair, and by no means would the strike of the stone be carried off to one side.
verses.20:17: Of the men of Israel also, apart from the sons of Benjamin, four hundred thousand were found who drew the sword and were prepared for battle.
verses.20:18: Rising up, they came to the house of God, that is, to Shiloh, and consulted God and said, "Who in our army will be the commander of the combat against the sons of Benjamin?" The Lord answered them, "Let Judah be your leader."
verses.20:19: And immediately the sons of Israel, rising in the morning, encamped near Gibeah;
verses.20:20: and advancing from there to battle against Benjamin, they began to assault the city.
verses.20:21: And the sons of Benjamin came out of Gibeah and killed twenty-two thousand men of the sons of Israel on that day.
verses.20:22: Again the sons of Israel, trusting both in their strength and in their number, drew up their battle line in the same place in which they had fought before,
verses.20:23: yet in such a way that first they went up and wept before the Lord until night, and consulted Him and said, "Should I advance further to fight against the sons of Benjamin, my brothers, or not?" He answered them, "Go up against them and enter into combat."
verses.20:24: And when on the second day the sons of Israel had advanced to battle against the sons of Benjamin,
verses.20:25: the sons of Benjamin burst out from the gates of Gibeah, and meeting them, raged against them with such great slaughter that they struck down eighteen thousand men who drew the sword.
verses.20:26: For this reason all the sons of Israel came to the house of God, and sitting down, they wept before the Lord; and they fasted on that day until evening, and offered to Him burnt offerings and peace offerings,
verses.20:27: and inquired concerning their situation. At that time the ark of the covenant of God was there,
verses.20:28: and Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, was in charge of the house. Therefore they consulted the Lord and said, "Should we go out further to battle against the sons of Benjamin, our brothers, or cease?" The Lord said to them, "Go up, for tomorrow I will deliver them into your hands."
verses.20:29: And the sons of Israel set ambushes all around the city of Gibeah,
verses.20:30: and for the third time, just as the first and second times, they led out the army against Benjamin.
verses.20:31: And the sons of Benjamin also boldly burst out from the city and pursued their fleeing adversaries quite far, so that they wounded some of them just as on the first day and the second, and cut down those turning their backs along the two paths, one of which led to Bethel and the other to Gibeah, and struck down about thirty men;
verses.20:32: for they thought that they were retreating in their usual manner. But the others, artfully feigning flight, had formed a plan to draw them away from the city and, as though fleeing, lead them to the paths mentioned above.
verses.20:33: Therefore all the sons of Israel, rising from their positions, stretched out their battle line in the place that is called Baal-tamar. The ambushes also, which were around the city, began gradually to reveal themselves
verses.20:34: and to advance from the western side of the city. Moreover, another ten thousand men from all Israel were provoking the inhabitants of the city to combat. And the war grew heavy against the sons of Benjamin, and they did not realize that destruction was pressing upon them from every side.
verses.20:35: And the Lord struck them in the sight of the sons of Israel, and on that day they killed twenty-five thousand one hundred men of them, all warriors and men who drew the sword.
verses.20:36: Now when the sons of Benjamin saw that they were weaker, they began to flee. Seeing this, the sons of Israel gave them room to flee, so that they might come to the prepared ambushes that they had placed near the city.
verses.20:37: When these had suddenly risen from their hiding places, and Benjamin was turning its back to those cutting them down, they entered the city and struck it with the edge of the sword.
verses.20:38: Now the sons of Israel had given a signal to those whom they had stationed in ambush, that after they had captured the city they should kindle a fire, so that by the smoke rising high they might show that the city was captured.
verses.20:39: When the sons of Israel positioned in the very combat saw this (for the sons of Benjamin thought they were fleeing and were pursuing more urgently, thirty men of their army having been cut down),
verses.20:40: and saw something like a column of smoke rising up from the city, and when Benjamin also, looking back, saw the city captured and the flames borne upward,
verses.20:41: those who had previously feigned flight turned their faces and resisted more strongly. When the sons of Benjamin saw this, they turned in flight
verses.20:42: and began to go toward the road of the desert, with their adversaries pursuing them there as well; moreover, those who had set fire to the city also met them.
verses.20:43: And so it came about that they were cut down by their enemies on both sides, nor was there any respite for the dying. They fell and were struck down on the eastern side of the city of Gibeah.
verses.20:44: Now those who were killed in that same place were eighteen thousand men, all very strong fighters.
verses.20:45: When those who remained of Benjamin saw this, they fled into the wilderness and were making their way toward the rock whose name is Rimmon. In that flight also, they killed five thousand men who were straggling and heading in different directions. And when they pushed on further, they pursued them and killed another two thousand as well.
verses.20:46: And so it came about that all who had fallen of Benjamin in various places were twenty-five thousand fighters, most ready for wars.
verses.20:47: Therefore six hundred men remained out of the entire number of Benjamin who were able to escape and flee into the wilderness, and they stayed at the rock of Rimmon for four months.
verses.20:48: Now the sons of Israel returned and struck with the sword all the remnants of the city, from men even to livestock, and a devouring flame consumed all the cities and villages of Benjamin.
verses.21:1: The sons of Israel also swore in Mizpah and said, "None of us will give any of his daughters as a wife to the sons of Benjamin."
verses.21:2: And they all came to the house of God in Shiloh, and sitting in His sight until evening, they lifted up their voice and with great wailing began to weep, saying,
verses.21:3: "Why, Lord God of Israel, has this evil happened among Your people, that today one tribe should be taken away from us?"
verses.21:4: Now on the next day, rising at daybreak, they built an altar and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings there, and said,
verses.21:5: "Who from all the tribes of Israel did not go up in the army of the Lord?" For they had bound themselves with a great oath when they were in Mizpah, that those who were absent should be put to death.
verses.21:6: And the sons of Israel, moved with remorse over their brother Benjamin, began to say, "One tribe has been taken away from Israel;
verses.21:7: from where will they take wives? For we have all sworn in common that we will not give them our daughters."
verses.21:8: Therefore they said, "Who is there from all the tribes of Israel who did not go up to the Lord in Mizpah?" And look, the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead were found not to have been in that army.
verses.21:9: (At that time also, when they were in Shiloh, none of them was found there.)
verses.21:10: Therefore they sent ten thousand very strong men and commanded them, "Go and strike the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead with the edge of the sword, both their wives and their little ones.
verses.21:11: And this will be what you must observe: kill every male and the women who have known men, but spare the virgins."
verses.21:12: And four hundred virgins were found from Jabesh-gilead who had not known a man's bed, and they brought them to the camp in Shiloh, in the land of Canaan.
verses.21:13: And they sent messengers to the sons of Benjamin who were at the rock of Rimmon, and commanded them to receive them in peace.
verses.21:14: And the sons of Benjamin came at that time, and wives from the daughters of Jabesh-gilead were given to them; but they did not find others whom they might hand over in a similar way.
verses.21:15: And all Israel grieved greatly and felt remorse over the slaughter of one tribe from Israel.
verses.21:16: And the elders said, "What shall we do for the rest, who have not received wives? All the women in Benjamin have fallen,
verses.21:17: and with great care and immense diligence we must see to it that one tribe is not blotted out from Israel.
verses.21:18: For we cannot give them our daughters, being bound by the oath and curse with which we said, 'Cursed is the one who gives any of his daughters as a wife to Benjamin.'"
verses.21:19: And they took counsel and said, "Look, there is an annual festival of the Lord in Shiloh, which is situated to the north of the city of Bethel, and on the eastern side of the road that leads from Bethel to Shechem, and to the south of the town of Lebonah."
verses.21:20: And they commanded the sons of Benjamin and said, "Go and hide in the vineyards.
verses.21:21: And when you see the daughters of Shiloh coming out according to custom to lead the dances, come out suddenly from the vineyards, and seize from among them each man a wife for himself, and go to the land of Benjamin.
verses.21:22: And when their fathers and brothers come and begin to complain and quarrel against you, we will say to them, 'Have pity on them, for they did not seize them by the right of warriors and victors; rather, when they asked to receive them, you did not give them, and the sin is on your part.'"
verses.21:23: And the sons of Benjamin did as they had been ordered, and according to their number they seized for themselves one wife each from those who were leading the dances; and they went away into their possession, building the cities and living in them.
verses.21:24: The sons of Israel also returned by tribes and families to their tents. In those days there was no king in Israel, but each one did what seemed right to himself.

notes.1:6: Latin summitatibus manuum ejus ac pedum literally reads "the extremities of his hands and feet" (likewise in 1:7), whereas the Hebrew specifies the thumbs and big toes.
notes.1:14: Latin suspirasset sedens in asino ("sighed while sitting on the donkey") reflects Jerome's understanding of the rare Hebrew verb tsanach, usually rendered as alighting from the donkey; similarly, in 1:11, 1:17, and 1:35 the Vulgate adds etymological glosses (civitas litterarum, anathema, and testaceo, reading Heres as "earthen" rather than "sun").
notes.1:19: Latin falcatis curribus ("scythed chariots") renders Hebrew "chariots of iron"; throughout 1:19-33 (and 2:3, 21), the Vulgate also uses delere ("wipe out/destroy," and interficere, "kill," in 1:29, 32) where the Hebrew has horish ("drive out/dispossess").
notes.1:23: Latin obsiderent ("were besieging") differs from the Hebrew, which says the house of Joseph sent spies to scout out Bethel.
notes.1:36: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew place names Akrabbim ("Scorpions") and Sela ("the rock") directly into Latin as ascensu Scorpionis ("ascent of the Scorpion," singular) and petra ("the rock").
notes.2:1: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew place name Bochim into Latin as Locum flentium ("the Place of Those Who Weep"), and adds the explanatory gloss sive lacrimarum ("or of Tears") in 2:5.
notes.2:3: Latin nolui delere... ut habeatis hostes, et dii eorum sint vobis in ruinam ("I was unwilling to wipe them out... so that you may have enemies, and their gods may be a ruin to you") differs from the Hebrew, which reads "I also said, I will not drive them out... they will be in your sides, and their gods will be a snare to you."
notes.2:5: The Clementine Vulgate reads the genitive hostias Domini ("sacrifices of the Lord," an objective genitive denoting offerings presented to the Lord) where the Hebrew and some Latin manuscripts have the dative "to the Lord."
notes.2:9: Latin Thamnathsare corresponds to "Timnath-serah" (agreeing with Joshua 19:50 and 24:31), whereas the Masoretic Text of Judges 2:9 reads "Timnath-heres."
notes.2:14: In the Vulgate, the plural relative clause qui ceperunt eos, et vendiderunt makes the plunderers the subject who captured and sold Israel to surrounding enemies, whereas in the Hebrew the Lord Himself is the subject who sold them; similarly, in 2:17 audientes mandata Domini, omnia fecere contraria applies to the rebellious Israelites rather than to their obedient fathers.
notes.3:10: The Vulgate renders Hebrew Aram-naharaim as Mesopotamia in 3:8 but as Syria here in 3:10, and reads 'in him' (in eo) where the Hebrew has 'upon him.'
notes.3:13: Latin copulavit ei uses the non-reflexive pronoun ('to him'), grammatically continuing the Lord as subject from 3:12, whereas the Hebrew is commonly read reflexively of Eglon ('he gathered to himself').
notes.3:15: Latin renders the Hebrew gentilic 'the Benjamite' literally as a patronymic (filii Jemini, 'the son of Jemini'), and interprets Hebrew 'restricted in his right hand' (left-handed) as ambidexterity ('used either hand as a right hand').
notes.3:16: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text specifies the sword's length as a gomed (a short cubit), the Vulgate describes a central hilt (in medio capulum) the length of the palm of a hand.
notes.3:31: Vulgate vomere ('with a plowshare') differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's 'with an oxgoad.'
notes.4:3: Vulgate falcatos currus ('scythed chariots,' also in 4:13) interprets the Hebrew 'chariots of iron' as chariots fitted with blades or scythes.
notes.4:6: The Vulgate presents Deborah's opening words as a direct statement ('has commanded you') rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text's rhetorical question ('Has not the Lord commanded?').
notes.4:11: Vulgate vallem, quae vocatur Sennim ('the valley that is called Sennim') differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's 'the oak in Zaanannim.'
notes.4:21: The Vulgate explicitly adds 'into his brain' (in cerebrum) and expresses Sisera's death as 'uniting deep sleep with death' (soporem morti consocians), where the Hebrew notes that he was fast asleep and exhausted.
notes.5:8: The Vulgate reads "The Lord chose new wars, and He Himself overthrew the gates of the enemies," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text is commonly rendered "they chose new gods; then war was in the gates." The conditional clause "if shield and spear appeared" reproduces a Hebraistic rhetorical idiom implying that none were seen.
notes.5:11: A distinctively Vulgate rendering ("Where the chariots were smashed together and the army of the enemies was suffocated... and obtained dominion"), diverging markedly from the obscure Hebrew text usually understood to mention singers or archers at the watering places.
notes.5:15: The Vulgate interprets Hebrew peluggot ("divisions" or "streams") as internal faction ("with Reuben divided against himself") and renders the following phrase as "a contention of great-hearted men was found," repeated in 5:16.
notes.5:18: The Vulgate takes the Hebrew phrase merome sadeh ("heights of the field") as a geographical proper name, in regione Merome ("in the region of Merome").
notes.5:21: The Vulgate renders Hebrew qedumim (commonly translated "ancient" or "onrushing") as a proper name, torrens Cadumim ("the torrent of Kedumim").
notes.6:11: The Vulgate divides the Hebrew gentilic avi ha-ezri ("the Abiezrite") literally as patrem familiae Ezri ("the father of the family of Ezri"; cf. 6:24), whereas 6:34 uses the form Abiezer. At the end of the verse, the Latin reads ut fugeret Madian ("in order to flee from Midian") rather than hiding the grain from Midian.
notes.6:24: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew altar name ("the Lord is peace") into Latin as Domini pax ("The Lord's Peace"), attaches "until the present day" to the naming, and joins "while he was still in Ophrah" to the Lord's nighttime command in 6:25.
notes.6:25: The Vulgate renders Hebrew ha-asherah (the Asherah pole) as nemus ("grove," also in 6:26, 30) and lucum ("sacred grove," 6:28), while distinguishing the Lord's altar (altare, 6:24, 26, 28) from Baal's altar (ara, 6:25, 28, 30-32).
notes.6:26: A distinctively Vulgate reading ("upon which you placed the sacrifice before"), whereas the Hebrew text directs that the altar be built "in proper order."
notes.6:31: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew clause commonly translated "whoever contends for him" as qui adversarius est ejus ("Whoever is his adversary"), preserving the literal Latin syntax of Joash's challenge.
notes.7:1: The Vulgate renders Hebrew gib'at ha-Moreh ('hill of Moreh') descriptively as collis excelsi ('the high hill') and has de nocte consurgens ('rising in the night') where the Hebrew says 'rising early.'
notes.7:3: Unlike the Hebrew, where departing from Mount Gilead is part of the proclamation, the Vulgate puts Recesseruntque de monte Galaad ('And they departed from Mount Gilead') in the past indicative as narrative.
notes.7:19: The Vulgate reads trecenti viri ('the three hundred men') rather than the Hebrew 'one hundred men' for the group entering the camp with Gideon, and specifies that they smashed the jars inter se ('against one another').
notes.7:23: The Vulgate omits 'toward Zererah' (present in the Hebrew after Beth-shittah) and reads in Tebbath ('in Tabbath').
notes.7:25: The Vulgate reads duos viros Madian ('two men of Midian') here rather than 'two princes of Midian' (contrast 8:3, where it uses principes).
notes.8:4: Whereas the Hebrew reads 'weary, yet pursuing,' the Vulgate reads et prae lassitudine, fugientes persequi non poterant ('and because of exhaustion, they were unable to pursue those who were fleeing').
notes.8:10: The Vulgate renders Hebrew ba-Karkor ('in Karkor') as the verb requiescebant ('were resting') rather than as a place name.
notes.8:13: The Vulgate translates Hebrew 'from the ascent of Heres' as ante solis ortum ('before the rising of the sun'), interpreting heres in its sense of 'sun.'
notes.8:32: The Vulgate reads de familia Ezri ('of the family of Ezri'), corresponding to the Hebrew 'of the Abiezrites' (cf. Abiezer in 8:2).
notes.8:33: Instead of retaining the proper name 'Baal-berith' as in the Hebrew, the Vulgate translates berit as a common noun in Percusseruntque cum Baal foedus ('And they made a covenant with Baal').
notes.9:9: Latin reads 'which both gods (dii) and men use (utuntur)' and 'be promoted (promovear) among the trees' (also vv. 11, 13), whereas the Hebrew speaks of honoring God/gods and men and swaying over the trees; Latin also distinguishes plural dii ('gods') here from singular Deum ('God') in v. 13.
notes.9:23: Latin reads Dominus ('the Lord') where the Hebrew has Elohim ('God'), and links vv. 23-24 syntactically so that the inhabitants of Shechem themselves begin to detest Abimelech and lay the killing of Jerubbaal's seventy sons upon him and the Shechemite rulers.
notes.9:26: Latin consistently gives the name of Gaal's father as Obed (vv. 26, 28, 30, 31, 35), whereas the Hebrew reads Ebed.
notes.9:28: Latin renders the clause concerning Zebul as a continuation of Gaal's rhetorical question ('and did he not appoint Zebul...'), whereas the Hebrew contains an imperative ('Serve the men of Hamor...'); in v. 29 Latin similarly has a passive ('And it was said to Abimelech') rather than Gaal continuing to speak.
notes.9:41: Latin reads in Ruma ('in Rumah'), reflecting a place name without the initial vowel of Hebrew Arumah.
notes.9:46: Latin reads 'their god Berith' (omitting El- of Hebrew El-berith) and includes an explanatory expansion ('where they had made a covenant with him, and from it the place had received its name; and it was very strongly fortified') interpreting the meaning of Berith ('covenant') and the fortified stronghold.
notes.10:1: The Vulgate reads 'dux in Israel' ('a leader in Israel') where the Hebrew has 'to save Israel,' and takes Hebrew 'ben-dodo' ('son of Dodo') as a common noun, rendering it 'patrui Abimelech' ('the uncle of Abimelech').
notes.10:4: The explanatory phrase 'id est, oppida Jair' ('that is, the towns of Jair') is a Vulgate gloss interpreting the Hebrew place-name Havvoth-jair.
notes.10:12: The Vulgate reads 'Chanaan' ('Canaan') where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'Maon' (the Maonites).
notes.11:19: The Vulgate reads 'usque ad fluvium' ('as far as the river,' i.e., the Jordan) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'to my place.'
notes.11:31: The Vulgate uses masculine personal pronouns ('quicumque primus ... eum,' 'whoever first ... him') and moves directly to 'him I will offer as a burnt offering to the Lord,' without the Hebrew's preceding clause 'shall be the Lord's.'
notes.11:33: The Vulgate translates the second element of the Hebrew place-name Abel-keramim as a relative clause: 'Abel, quae est vineis consita' ('Abel, which is planted with vineyards').
notes.11:35: The Vulgate renders Jephthah's exclamation as 'decepisti me, et ipsa decepta es' ('you have deceived me, and you yourself have been deceived') where the Hebrew reads 'you have brought me very low, and you have become among those who trouble me.'
notes.11:40: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew verb 'letannot' (often understood as 'to commemorate' or 'to recount') as 'plangant' ('mourn' or 'lament'), matching 'plangam' in 11:37.
notes.12:1: Vulgate reads orta est seditio ("an uprising arose") and contra aquilonem ("toward the north"), translating the place name Zaphon by its Hebrew meaning "north" and omitting the Hebrew closing phrase "over you with fire."
notes.12:5: Latin reads Ephrathaeus ("Ephrathite"), Jerome's transliteration of the Hebrew gentilic Ephrati, which here denotes a member of the tribe of Ephraim.
notes.12:6: Vulgate adds the explanatory glosses quod interpretatur Spica ("which means 'ear of grain'") and eadem littera spicam exprimere non valens ("not being able to pronounce 'ear of grain' with the same letter") to clarify the pronunciation test between Scibboleth and Sibboleth.
notes.12:7: Vulgate reads the singular in civitate sua Galaad ("in his city, Gilead"), whereas the Hebrew text reads "in the cities of Gilead."
notes.12:11: Vulgate names the judge Ahialon (Aijalon), where the Hebrew vocalizes the name as Elon; in 12:12 it states simply in Zabulon ("in Zebulun"), omitting the Hebrew place name "in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun."
notes.13:5: Vulgate includes the doublet ab infantia sua et ex matris utero ("from his infancy and from his mother's womb," repeated in v. 7), where the Hebrew text reads simply "from the womb."
notes.13:6: Vulgate states that the woman asked the visitor who he was, where he had come from, and his name, and he was unwilling to tell her; the Hebrew text instead states that she did not ask where he was from, and he did not tell her his name.
notes.13:19: Vulgate renders Hebrew minchah ("grain offering") as libamenta ("drink offerings," also in v. 23), and makes qui facit mirabilia ("who performs wonders") a relative clause describing the Lord rather than an action performed by the angel during the offering.
notes.13:25: Vulgate reads esse cum eo ("to be with him"), whereas the Hebrew text reads "to stir him" or "to impel him."
notes.14:6: Clementine Vulgate prints in frustra, a traditional spelling variant of in frusta ("into pieces").
notes.14:8: Vulgate specifically places the swarm of bees in ore leonis ("in the mouth of the lion"), whereas the Hebrew text reads "in the carcass/body of the lion" (compare de corpore leonis in v. 9).
notes.14:10: Vulgate makes Samson's father the subject who gave the feast (fecit filio suo Samson convivium, "made a feast for his son Samson"), whereas the Hebrew text states that Samson himself made the feast there.
notes.14:20: Vulgate makes Samson's wife the active subject (accepit maritum, "took as a husband"), whereas the Hebrew text uses a passive construction ("was given to").
notes.15:8: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew idiom 'hip upon thigh' (denoting ruthless slaughter) as a result clause describing the Philistines' astonishment: 'so that, stunned, they placed calf upon thigh' (ita ut stupentes suram femori imponerent).
notes.15:16: Where the Hebrew plays on the word chamor ('donkey'/'heap') as 'heaps upon heaps,' the Vulgate renders a poetic parallel: 'with the lower jaw of the colt of female donkeys, I have destroyed them' (in mandibula pulli asinarum, delevi eos).
notes.15:17: The Vulgate adds 'singing' (canens) and supplies an explanatory Latin gloss for the Hebrew place name Ramath-lehi ('Lifting Up of the Jawbone,' Elevatio maxillæ), as it also does for Lehi in verse 9.
notes.15:19: The Vulgate understands Hebrew makhtesh ('hollow' or 'tooth socket') as 'a molar tooth in the jawbone of the donkey' (molarem dentem in maxilla asini) rather than a hollow in the ground at Lehi, and translates the place name En-hakkore as 'Spring of the One Calling from the Jawbone.'
notes.16:8: The Latin text reads eam ('her') here, evidently a slip for eum ('him'), which the context and the following verse require.
notes.16:13: Like the Septuagint, the Vulgate includes the instruction about fastening the woven hair with a peg (clavum) driven into the ground, a clause absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.16:17: The Vulgate renders Hebrew morah ('razor') as 'iron' (Ferrum) and adds the explanatory gloss 'that is, consecrated to God' (id est, consecratus Deo) for 'Nazirite.'
notes.16:28: The Vulgate reads 'restore to me now my former strength' and 'for the loss of my two eyes' (pro amissione duorum luminum, literally 'two lights'), whereas the Hebrew has 'strengthen me just this once' and 'for one of my two eyes.'
notes.17:2: Where the Hebrew reads 'that were taken from you, and about which you uttered a curse,' the Vulgate reads 'that you had set apart for yourself, and over which you had sworn' (quos separaveras tibi, et super quibus ... juraveras).
notes.17:5: The Vulgate inserts an explanatory gloss for 'ephod and teraphim' ('that is, a priestly garment and idols') and preserves the literal idiom 'filled the hand' (implevit ... manum, also in verse 12), meaning to ordain or install as a priest.
notes.17:10: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew 'suit of clothes' as 'a double garment' (vestem duplicem).
notes.17:13: The Vulgate reads 'God' (Deus) here, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has the divine name YHWH ('the Lord').
notes.18:7: Vulgate "of great wealth" (magnarumque opum) reflects an interpretation of a difficult Hebrew phrase for a magistrate or ruler as referring to abundant treasure.
notes.18:12: Vulgate translates the Hebrew place name Mahaneh-dan directly into Latin as Castrorum Dan ("Camp of Dan").
notes.18:27: Vulgate summarizes the objects taken from Micah as "the things we mentioned above" (quae supra diximus), where the Hebrew reads "what Micah had made."
notes.18:30: Vulgate reads "son of Moses" (filii Moysi) and "their captivity" (captivitatis suae), whereas the Masoretic Hebrew reads "Manasseh" (with a suspended letter nun) and "the captivity of the land."
notes.18:31: The Clementine Vulgate places "In those days there was no king in Israel" at the end of 18:31 rather than at the opening of 19:1 as in the Hebrew text.
notes.19:2: Vulgate reads "who left him" (quae reliquit eum), aligning with a Septuagint tradition rather than the Masoretic Hebrew "was unfaithful to him"; in 19:1, 19:9, and 19:29 the Vulgate also calls her "wife" (uxor) alongside "concubine" (concubina) elsewhere in the chapter.
notes.19:16: Vulgate preserves the distinct form "sons of Jemini" (filii Jemini, reflecting Hebrew bene yemini, meaning Benjaminites), contrasting with "Benjamin" in 19:14.
notes.19:18: Vulgate reads "the house of God" (domum Dei), where the Masoretic Hebrew has "the house of the Lord" and the Septuagint "my house."
notes.19:22: The parenthetical gloss "(that is, without a yoke)" (id est, absque jugo) is Jerome's etymological explanation of Belial embedded directly in the Vulgate text.
notes.19:24: Vulgate explicitly renders the Hebrew "this disgraceful thing" as "this crime against nature" (scelus hoc contra naturam), and similarly renders Hebrew "know" as "abuse" (abutamur) in 19:22.
notes.20:2: Latin anguli populorum ("corners of the peoples") literally renders the Hebrew idiom pinnoth, referring to the chiefs or pillars of the tribes.
notes.20:15: The Vulgate reads viginti quinque millia ("twenty-five thousand"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads twenty-six thousand.
notes.20:16: The Vulgate describes these seven hundred men as ambidextrous (ita sinistra ut dextra praeliantes, "fighting with the left hand just as with the right"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text describes them as left-handed.
notes.20:18: The Vulgate translates Hebrew Beth-el as the appellative domum Dei ("the house of God") and adds the gloss hoc est, in Silo ("that is, to Shiloh"), a reading also reflected in 20:26 and 21:2.
notes.20:36: In the Vulgate, Benjamin begins to flee and Israel gives them room to flee toward the ambush, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text states that Israel gave ground to Benjamin because they relied on the ambush.
notes.21:2: As in 20:18, the Vulgate renders Hebrew Beth-el as domum Dei ("the house of God") and explicitly locates it in Silo ("in Shiloh"); compare also the mention of Shiloh in 21:9.
notes.21:10: The Vulgate reads decem millia ("ten thousand"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads twelve thousand.
notes.21:22: On a difficult Hebrew clause, the Vulgate gives a distinct sense: Benjamin did not seize the women by right of war, rather the families incurred sin by withholding them when asked.
notes.21:24: The Clementine Vulgate combines verses 24 and 25 of the Hebrew Masoretic Text into a single verse 21:24.
